jobs.title: SCI - Research Administrator 3  (Remote)
jobs.description: This Research Administrator position will be home based from anywhere within the United States** The Stanford Cancer Institute (SCI) is currently seeking a Senior Research Administrator to facilitate the growth of its research. The candidate will bring extensive Stanford experience and be a key member of the research administration team, working to manage the proposal preparation and post award activities on grants, contracts, program projects, and federal grants, both routine and complex. This position will also involve financial analysis and forecasting for research activities. The individual will be a liaison among faculty, central research administration offices, and the department finance team. The ideal candidate should enjoy interacting and working with many different people and teams, be able to follow through in a fast-paced environment, adapt well to changing priorities, anticipate and plan for tight funding situations, employ critical thinking in daily tasks, and be a self-starter. SCI is an NCI-Designated Comprehensive Cancer Center that integrates key strengths in cancer biology, immunology, genetics, population sciences and clinical oncology with expertise in imaging, engineering and technology development. The translation of basic science discoveries through clinical trials and collaborative team science is a distinguishing feature of the SCI. This position will directly support the pre- and post-award administration for several SCI Faculty. These portfolios include a wide range of sponsors i.e. federal, non-federal and industry as well as award types including but not limited to: grants, contracts, cooperative agreements, subawards, both incoming and outgoing, fellowships, etc. NCI-designated Cancer Centers serve as major sources of discovery into the nature of cancer and of the development of more effective approaches to prevention, diagnosis, and therapy. They contribute significantly to the development of Shared Resources that support cancer relevant research and they collaborate and coordinate their research efforts with other NCI-funded programs and investigators. Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. -OR- B. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico. 3. Qualifications: You must meet both the Basic Requirement and the Specialized Experience to qualify for this series as described below. BASIC REQUIREMENT: A. Degree: physical science, engineering, or mathematics that included 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science such as mechanics, dynamics, properties of materials, and electronics. OR B. Combination of education and experience: education equivalent to one of the majors shown in A above that included at least 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science, plus appropriate experience or additional education. GS-15 SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS: A qualified candidate's online application and resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-14 in the Federal service. Specialized experience for this position is defined as meeting 2 of 3 of the following: Leading and managing complex, multi-phase engineering or scientific programs/projects from conception through completion, including establishing project schedules, baselines, and resource allocations. Applying advanced engineering or physical science principles and conducting extensive technical analyses to resolve novel, highly complex, and unstructured problems where precedents are often lacking. Developing long-range operational plans, goals, and strategic frameworks to guide major technical initiatives and ensure alignment with organizational objectives. GS-14 SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS: A qualified candidate's online application and resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-13 in the Federal service. Specialized experience for this position is defined as meeting 2 of 3 of the following: Planning, organizing, and managing complex engineering or scientific projects, studies, or program segments that involve technical uncertainty, diverse requirements, or lack established precedents. Evaluating technical alternatives, conducting engineering or scientific analyses, and developing practical solutions to complex, unstructured problems where existing guidelines have gaps or are inapplicable. Serving as a technical authority or expert advisor, providing authoritative consultation, technical input, and recommendations to management, colleagues, or external stakeholders on significant engineering or scientific matters. "Experience" refers to paid and unpaid experience. Examples of qualifying unpaid experience may include: volunteer work done through National Service programs (such as Peace Corps and AmeriCorps); as well as work for other community-based philanthropic and social organizations. Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills; and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. You must meet all qualifications and eligibility requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

jobs.title: Supervisory Physical Scientist
jobs.description: This position is part of the Advanced Mining and Mineral Production Technologies Office, within the Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation (CMEI), within the U.S. Department of Energy. As a Supervisory Physical Scientist, you will lead the Resource Characterization Technologies Program, the Mining and Extraction Technologies Program, or the Mineral and Extractive Metallurgical Processing Technologies Program. Qualifications: You must meet both the Basic Requirement and the Specialized Experience to qualify for this series as described below. BASIC REQUIREMENT: A. Degree: physical science, engineering, or mathematics that included 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science such as mechanics, dynamics, properties of materials, and electronics. OR B. Combination of education and experience: education equivalent to one of the majors shown in A above that included at least 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science, plus appropriate experience or additional education. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS: A qualified candidate's online application and resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-14 in the Federal service. Specialized experience for this position is defined as meeting 2 of the 3 of the following: Directing or managing large-scale engineering, physical science, or technical programs/projects characterized by high complexity, multiple phases, and diverse operational or regulatory requirements. Serving as a recognized senior technical authority or consultant, providing authoritative advice and guidance to senior management, technical staff, and external stakeholders on complex, novel, or controversial engineering and scientific issues. Planning and overseeing project budgets, resource allocations, schedules, and contractor performance while ensuring adherence to safety, environmental, and technical quality standards. "Experience" refers to paid and unpaid experience. Examples of qualifying unpaid experience may include: volunteer work done through National Service programs (such as Peace Corps and AmeriCorps); as well as work for other community-based philanthropic and social organizations. Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills; and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. CTAP/ICTAP candidates: To be considered "well qualified" you must meet all of the requirements as described in this section. You must meet all qualifications and eligibility requirements by the closing date of this announcement. The incumbent will work in one of the programs within the Advanced Mining and Mineral Production Technologies Office. Resource Characterization Program Expert mastery and demonstrated skills in some combination of the following: Knowledge of state-of-the-art technologies for mineral resource characterization and prospecting including techniques for identifying, evaluating, and de-risking domestic mineral resources through advanced geoscience, analytical tools, and data-driven resource evaluation and characterization approaches. Ability to assess technical approaches for the identification, detection, and estimation of mineral resources and approaches to understanding recoverability and valuation. Demonstrated skills related to collaboration and coordination as a technical interface with mining communities, state and/or industry partners and other federal agencies. Abilities to evaluate cutting edge technologies in geoscience, subsurface engineering, and marine technology deployment. Mining and Extraction Program Expert mastery and demonstrated skills in some combination of the following: Ability to assess mine technologies, including tools that improve mine planning, fleet management, energy use, throughput, maintenance, logistics, and overall system performance. Skill in evaluating technical maturity, scalability, cost, deployment barriers, safety implications, and commercial relevance of emerging mining technologies such as in situ mining and marine minerals. Ability to synthesize technical, economic, operational, and strategic information to inform major public-sector investment decisions in mining systems and minerals supply chains. Ability to understand mining as an integrated system involving geology, extraction, equipment, labor, safety, processing, logistics, energy, permitting, and economics. Processing and Extractive Metallurgy Program Expert mastery and demonstrated skills in some combination of the following: Knowledge of established physical, thermodynamic, and chemical approaches in mineral processing or extractive metallurgy including, hydrometallurgy, pyrometallurgy, biological and other advanced chemical approaches. Skills in evaluating technologies suitable for unit operations as well as circuit, flowsheet, and system process analysis. Ability to understand and communicate mineral production economics including byproduct dependencies and product market characteristics. Abilities and experience in designing, operating, or managing mineral production systems, innovations, or R&D efforts for improving mineral production operations. Knowledge of mining industry operations, economic and financial considerations, and technology adoption.

jobs.description: LEVEL: Mid-Level LOCATION : Arlington, VA or St. Petersburg, FL - hybrid preferred, however exceptional fully remote candidates will be considered TYPE: Full time regular employment, with benefits DEADLINE: Friday, 20 November 2026 @ 5:00pm EST McColm & Company (McColm) is a mission-driven, customer-focused professional services firm that equips change makers with the knowledge, skills, and insights they need to succeed in an increasingly complex world. We manage bespoke professional training programs, deliver capacity-building solutions, and provide specialized technical assistance, research, and evaluation expertise to decision makers. McColm’s Justice and Resilience Practice supports clients working to ensure the effectiveness and outcomes of training and technical assistance projects that address human trafficking and forced labor. McColm issues this Call for CVs for qualified Instructional Systems Designer candidates under an anticipated contract. Lead instructional design support for the program’s online and live national training offerings and other approved T/TA offerings. Apply adult learning principles and e-learning best practices to face-to-face, virtual, self-directed, and blended learning formats. Support the development and maintenance of instructor guides, Training of Trainers materials, reference materials, and other instructional resources. Support learning management system implementation and troubleshooting, and ensure instructional products address applicable accessibility, technical, and accreditation requirements. Coordinate with the Evaluation Specialist to use learner assessments, participant feedback, and other empirical data to improve instructional products. Communicate effectively, orally and in writing, with Government personnel, project staff, subject matter experts, and the audiences the program serves. Requirements The qualified candidate for the Instructional Systems Designer role must possess the following: Bachelor’s degree and at least 8 years of relevant experience, or Master’s degree and at least 6 years of relevant experience. Instructional design certification from an accredited institution, or at least 10 years of directly relevant instructional design experience. Experience developing multidisciplinary T/TA for customers that educates social services, health care, behavioral health, and public health professionals to respond to the needs of impacted populations, including survivors of human trafficking. At least 5 years of experience as a facilitator. Demonstrated experience identifying performance gaps or learning needs. Demonstrated experience formally documenting instructional design plans. Demonstrated experience using empirical data to make instructional design decisions. Demonstrated experience ensuring that instructional solutions address performance gaps. Demonstrated experience identifying and implementing improvements to instruction. Demonstrated experience designing instructional strategies that engage and motivate learners and use learner-centered approaches. Demonstrated experience using face-to-face, online, and blended learning strategies. Demonstrated experience developing project management plans for instructional design projects. Demonstrated experience designing assessments of learning. Demonstrated experience collaborating across functional teams. Experience with online learning platforms and tools. jobs.title: Statistician
jobs.description: Joining the Secret Service, Office of Human Resources, will allow you to be responsible for aggregating, collating, and analyzing human capital data across complex situations. For definitions of terms found in this announcement, please click here. Qualifications: To be considered qualified for this position you must meet the following qualification requirements for the respective grade level in which you are applying. Applicants must demonstrate that they meet the Basic Requirements AND Minimum Qualification requirements as listed below: BASIC REQUIREMENTS: A. Degree: that included 15 semester hours in statistics (or in mathematics and statistics, provided at least 6 semester hours were in statistics), and 9 additional semester hours in one or more of the following: physical or biological sciences, medicine, education, or engineering; or in the social sciences including demography, history, economics, social welfare, geography, international relations, social or cultural anthropology, health sociology, political science, public administration, psychology, etc. OR B. Combination of education and experience -- courses as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. The experience should have included a full range of professional statistical work such as (a)sampling, (b) collecting, computing, and analyzing statistical data, and (c) applying statistical techniques such as measurement of central tendency, dispersion, skewness, sampling error, simple and multiple correlation, analysis of variance, and tests of significance. IN ADDITION TO MEETING THE BASIC REQUIREMENTS ABOVE, YOU MUST ALSO MEET THE FOLLOWING MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: You qualify for the GS-13 level if you possess one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 level performing duties such as: Applying statistical, mathematical, and analytical techniques to analyze human capital and/or workforce management data. Producing reports, visualizations or dashboards utilizing statistical and data management tools (e.g. Excel, SAS, Python, Power BI or Cognos). Interpreting analytical results and preparing written products and briefings to inform human capital and/or workforce-management You qualify for the GS-14 level if you possess one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 level performing duties such as: Applying statistical methods and sophisticated analytical techniques, such as multivariate regression, time series analysis, and predictive modeling, to analyze and interpret large human capital and/or workforce-management datasets. Leading statistical analyses and research models to evaluate and forecast federal human capital outcomes. Producing technical products, dashboards or executive-level analytical briefings utilizing statistical and data management tools (e.g. Excel, SAS, Python, Power BI or Cognos). Establishing analytical methodologies, standards, and/or internal operating procedures for statistical research and human capital analytics. The qualification requirements listed above must be met by the closing date of this announcement. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Current or Former Political Appointees: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) must authorize employment offers made to current or former political appointees. If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES or Presidential Appointee employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the Human Resources Office.

jobs.title: Group Curriculum Manager, Science
jobs.description:
About Amplify

Amplify helps teachers bring delight and rigor to students every day. We have become a leader in K–12 literacy, biliteracy, math, and science by building inspiring teaching and learning experiences based on research. The Amplify Classroom platform combines curriculum, assessment, and supplemental learning into one coherent high-quality instructional system. A pioneer in education since 2000, Amplify has developed deep relationships in states and districts by partnering with educators to drive implementation quality and improved outcomes. Today, Amplify serves more than 18 million students and teachers across all 50 states and on six continents. For more information, visit Amplify.com http://amplify.com.



As a Group Curriculum Manager, you will manage a content development team responsible for creating and reviewing curriculum materials for Amplify Science, grades K-8. This management role requires curriculum expertise as well as people leadership and operational oversight to ensure consistent, high-quality educational content delivery across curriculum programs.

 

Job Responsibilities:

 - Manage content development team and operations - directly manage a team of Curriculum Content Specialists and Copy Editors, providing day-to-day leadership, performance management, professional development, and resource coordination to ensure effective content production across multiple curriculum areas.

 - Oversee multi-curriculum content development - coordinate content creation across internal and external teams across grade levels, ensuring consistent quality standards, alignment with academic requirements, and timely delivery of comprehensive instructional materials that meet diverse educational needs.

 - Drive content quality and consistency standards - establish and maintain content development processes, review procedures, and quality benchmarks that ensure all educational materials meet organizational standards and educational effectiveness requirements across all curriculum programs.

 - Coordinate project delivery and resource management - manage content development timelines, allocate team resources across multiple curriculum projects, and ensure successful delivery of educational materials within scope and deadline requirements while maintaining quality standards.

 - Develop team capabilities and performance - provide coaching and mentoring to content specialists, conduct performance evaluations, identify skill development opportunities, and foster professional growth while building team expertise across diverse curriculum areas.

 - Facilitate collaboration and content integration - work with curriculum teams, subject matter experts, and educational stakeholders to ensure seamless content alignment, coordinate cross-curricular initiatives, and maintain consistency across all educational programs and materials.

 - Monitor content effectiveness and improvement - track content performance through educator feedback and student outcome data, identify areas for enhancement, and implement improvements that increase educational impact and instructional effectiveness.

 

How You Work...

 - You excel at team management and operational execution - effectively leading content professionals while coordinating complex projects across multiple curriculum areas, ensuring both team performance and content delivery meet organizational expectations.

 - You balance people leadership with content expertise - maintaining deep understanding of subject matter expertise and curriculum development while focusing on team development, performance management, and creating collaborative environments that produce exceptional educational content.

 - You drive consistent results across diverse content areas - ensuring quality and effectiveness standards are maintained across various subjects and grade levels while adapting management approaches to meet specific curriculum requirements and team needs.

 

Basic Qualifications:

 - 8+ years of progressive science curriculum content development experience, including 3-5 years of increasing management responsibility with documented success leading content teams, managing multiple curriculum projects, and delivering high-quality educational materials across diverse subject areas.

 - Bachelor's degree in Science, Education, Curriculum and Instruction, or related field required. Master's degree is highly preferred.

 - Proven people management and team leadership experience - demonstrated success managing science content development professionals, conducting performance evaluations, providing coaching and development, and building collaborative team environments that drive content excellence.

 - Multi-curriculum project management expertise - proven ability to coordinate content development across various subject areas and grade levels, manage competing priorities and timelines, and ensure consistent quality and delivery standards.

 - Content development operations experience - hands-on understanding of curriculum development processes, quality assurance procedures, and content review workflows with ability to optimize team productivity and content effectiveness.

 - Strong communication and collaboration skills - exceptional ability to work with diverse stakeholders, facilitate team meetings, provide clear feedback and direction, and maintain effective working relationships across curriculum programs.

 - Educational standards and assessment knowledge - thorough understanding of academic standards, curriculum alignment requirements, and assessment integration with ability to ensure content meets educational objectives and compliance requirements.

 - Team development and coaching abilities - experience mentoring curriculum professionals, identifying skill gaps, providing professional development opportunities, and building team capabilities across diverse content areas.

 - Data analysis and improvement focus - ability to analyze content effectiveness data, gather stakeholder feedback, and implement targeted improvements that enhance educational outcomes and team performance.

Amplify is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Description:

The Revenue Systems Analyst is the connective tissue between Revenue Systems, the overall Revenue Operations team, and the Business Systems team. This role leads structured process discovery, maps current and future state workflows, and translates operational needs into clear, testable requirements for Business Systems and other partners, with a focus on business clarity rather than system configuration. The focus of the Revenue Systems team is improving seller and sales-operations execution across lead-to-cash (quoting, contracting, ordering, invoicing, renewals/amendments), reducing rework, strengthening data integrity, sales finance/ budgeting, and accelerating change adoption.

This role also supports the strategy, administration, and adoption of the platforms that power revenue workflows, including our market intelligence platform. Success in this role depends less on producing documents than on the human work behind them, building trust with business partners, asking the questions that surface what people actually do versus what the process says they do, and driving decisions across teams that don't always agree. This is not a system administration or configuration role.



Essential Responsibilities:



Business Process Discovery and Design

 - Facilitate workshops and working sessions with key stakeholders (Account Executives, District Managers, Sales Support, Renewals, Sales Finance, and Business Systems) to document current state end-to-end business processes and define improved future state designs facilitated by systems and process improvements.

 - Create clear, multi-level process maps (e.g., lead-to-quote, quote-to-contract, order-to-cash, renewals/amendments) that reflect real seller and operations workflows, handoffs, approvals, and exception paths.

 - Establish and maintain a lightweight process library (maps, SOPs, definitions, decision trees) so institutional knowledge is durable and scalable.

Requirements and Solution Definition (Sales and Sales Operations Lens)

 - Translate process and policy decisions into well-structured requirements: user stories, acceptance criteria, business rules, and operational scenarios - ensuring clarity, completeness, and testability.

 - Partner with Business Systems to validate feasibility, clarify ambiguities, and ensure requirements reflect both the operational intent and system constraints.

 - Maintain traceability from process maps -> requirements -> test cases -> release notes to reduce rework and ensure end-to-end quality.

 - Use AI-powered tools (e.g., Glean, Claude, Gemini) to accelerate drafting of user stories, business cases, acceptance criteria, process documentation, and stakeholder synthesis — applying judgment to validate accuracy, completeness, and business fit rather than accepting output at face value.

Tools Strategy and Administration

 - Support the administration and strategy development of the platforms supporting revenue workflows, including our market intelligence platform, assisting in configuration, user access, adoption tracking, and vendor coordination.

 - Translate market intelligence signals into usable seller and sales-operations workflows, partnering with Business Systems on data flow, attribution, and reporting integration.

 - Build and maintain enablement resources (playbooks, prompt libraries, use case guides) that drive consistent, high-value usage across the field.

 - Evaluate, pilot, and operationalize additional platforms as needed, including AI-enabled solutions, and make recommendations on fit, sequencing, and expansion.

Operational Readiness, Testing, and Change Enablement

 - Co-design UAT approaches and test scenarios rooted in real-world seller and Sales Operations use cases; coordinate execution with Business Systems and key business testers.

 - Develop end-user documentation (job aids, playbooks, process guides) and support enablement activities to drive adoption and consistent execution.

 - Support release readiness by confirming training, communications, reporting impacts, and operational 'go-live' checklists are complete.

Continuous Improvement and Performance Insights

 - Use operational data and qualitative feedback to identify friction points, bottlenecks, policy leakage, and process variability - and recommend improvements.

 - Support defining process KPIs (cycle time, rework/defect rates, adoption, SLA attainment) and partner with reporting teams to surface actionable insights.

 - Promote standardization and simplification while preserving necessary state/district/contracting complexity through clear guardrails and exception handling.

 - Evaluate emerging technologies, automation opportunities, and AI-enabled solutions that can simplify workflows, reduce manual effort, and improve operational effectiveness.

Cross-Functional Partnership and Governance

 - Act as a neutral facilitator to align Sales, Finance, and Business Systems on process decisions, definitions, and sequencing - especially in quoting, contracting, ordering, and invoicing workflows.

 - Support governance routines (change intake, prioritization, documentation standards, decision logs) to keep cross-functional work moving and reduce 'spin.'

 - Contribute to program initiatives across the revenue systems roadmap (e.g., quoting modernization, amendments/contracting improvements, data governance, commission and budget operationalization, seller enablement).

Minimum Qualifications:

 - Bachelor's degree in Business, Operations, or related field (or equivalent experience).

 - 4+ years of experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Business Process Analysis, or related roles focused on process design and operational improvement.

 - Demonstrated ability to create process maps and documentation that non-technical audiences can follow (e.g., Lucidchart, Visio, Miro, or similar).

 - Experience translating business needs into clear requirements (user stories, acceptance criteria, business rules) and supporting cross-functional delivery.

 - Experience working with CRM and revenue operations platforms (Salesforce preferred) and familiarity with lead-to-cash processes including quoting, contracting, ordering, invoicing, and renewals.

 - Strong facilitation, stakeholder management, and written communication skills; comfortable driving alignment across teams with competing priorities.

 - Analytical mindset and comfort using data to diagnose issues and validate improvements.

 - Demonstrated curiosity and willingness to learn new technologies, methodologies, and ways of working, including the use of AI-powered tools to improve productivity, process design, analysis, documentation, and decision-making.



Travel required (about 10-15%).



Preferred Qualifications:

jobs.description: Advocates For Children (AFC) is a dynamic social justice organization that strives to ensure a high-quality education for New York students who face barriers to academic success, focusing on students from low-income backgrounds. AFC works on behalf of children and youth who are at greatest risk of academic failure due to poverty, race, ethnicity, disability, homelessness, immigration status/limited English proficiency, or involvement in the child welfare or juvenile/criminal legal systems. We use uniquely integrated strategies to advance systemic reform, empower families and communities, and advocate for the educational rights of individual students. AFC grounds our work in our organization’s values: Family-Centered: We listen to what families want for their children and empower them with information and support. Expertise: W e ground our advocacy in more than 50 years of experience with the NYC public schools and deep knowledge of the legal and education systems affecting the students and families we serve. Passion: We are united by our unrelenting drive to dismantle obstacles to education and our unwavering dedication to NYC’s students and families. Community: We foster collaboration and inclusive practices within our team and with outside partners so we can learn from different perspectives and unite in advancing our common goals. Justice: We view the law as a powerful tool to bridge gaps in access to education and help families from under-represented communities fight for their rights. Impact: We recognize that our value lies in the difference we make in the lives of students and their families and push ourselves to achieve concrete results. For more information on AFC, see www.advocatesforchildren.org . JOB SUMMARY AFC seeks an Education Advocate in our Immigrant Students' Rights Project (ISRP). ISRP works to protect the education-related rights of underserved immigrant families. Immigrant families face unique obstacles in NYC public schools related to their linguistic and cultural backgrounds. We are looking for an advocate to join our team to serve immigrant families of children with disabilities and English Language Learners (ELLs). The Education Advocate will report directly to ISRP's Project Director. PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Assisting families with school related issues such as special education, school enrollment, bilingual programs, and bullying. Conducting intakes of new clients. Participating in school meetings and school visits. Providing know-your-rights trainings to families across New York City and staffing tables at information fairs. Locating and connecting families with resources in their communities. Drafting and updating informational materials for immigrant parents. Supporting ISRP policy advocacy efforts as needed. QUALIFICATIONS Understanding of and alignment with AFC’s mission. Please review AFC’s work at www.advocatesforchildren.org . Desire to learn, both as an individual and as part of an organization, and apply diversity, equity, inclusion, and anti-racism principles. A bachelor's degree. Fluency in Spanish. Organized, detail oriented, and able to work independently on tasks and deliverables . Experience working with families is preferred. Strong presentation skills and comfort with public speaking. Strong writing ability and analytical skills. Ability to explain complex concepts in a manner that is easy to understand. Ability to multi-task and respond to changing needs. Available to work occasional evenings and weekends and to travel within the five boroughs. Proficient in Microsoft Office programs: Word, Outlook, SharePoint . APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS Candidates should submit a resume and cover letter highlighting why they are interested in this role at AFC and how their experience aligns with the Education Advocate position, including any personal or profession al experience that demonstrates your connection to the populations that AFC serves. The position is available starting in August 2026, and resumes will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Due to the high volume of applicants, only qualified candidates will be contacted. COMPENSATION This is a full-time position, with a salary in the range of $63,702 - $69,323, depending on experience, and includes a comprehensive benefits package. This position is expected to work at least 2 days a week in the office and remotely on the remaining days. ADDITIONAL COMPENSATION INFORMATION AFC’s current compensation package includes medical and dental insurance, with a plan option that covers full payment of medical plan premiums for staff and their qualified dependents . AFC has generous time-off policies that include 10 federal holidays, office closure between Christmas and New Year’s Day, and 15 vacation days and 15 paid time off days in the first year of employment . AFC also offers a 403(b) plan with a fully vested employer match and coverage of the premium cost of life insurance and short-term and long-term disability insurance. AFC is an equal opportunity employer that actively seeks to recruit and retain a diverse staff and encourages all applications including from people of color, persons with disabilities, parents of persons with disabilities, persons of diverse sexual orientations, gender identities or gender expressions and persons of diverse socioeconomic backgrounds. AFC is committed to providing access, equal opportunity, and reasonable accommodation when requested by a qualified applicant or employee with a disability or other protected characteristic. The policy regarding requests for reasonable accommodation applies to all aspects of employment, including the application process. For more information and to request an accommodation, contact Human Resources at HR@advocatesforchildren.org .

jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. Anthropic Fellows Program overview The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience. Fellows will primarily use external infrastructure (e.g. open-source models, public APIs) to work on project aligned with our research priorities, with the goal of producing a public output (e.g. a paper submission). In one of our earlier cohorts, over 80% of fellows produced papers. We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis. Submit your application to the Economics & Policy workstream at the bottom of this page. We are accepting applications on a rolling basis for the next cohort expected to start in January 2027. In some circumstances, we can accommodate fellows starting outside the usual cohort timelines — please note in your application if the January 2027 start date doesn't work for you. What to expect 4 months of full-time research Direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers Weekly stipend of 4,615 USD / 3,440 GBP / 6,470 CAD / 4,110 EUR + benefits (these vary by country) Substantial funding for compute and other research expenses Interview process The interview process will include an initial application, assessments, and interviews. We may ask for references later in the process as well. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Compensation The expected base stipend for this role is 4,615 USD / 3,440 GBP / 6,470 CAD / 4,110 EUR per week, with an expectation of 40 hours per week for 4 months (with possible extension). The Anthropic Institute Fellows (Economics & Policy) Mentors, research areas, & past projects Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential research areas and mentors include: Economics Maxim Massenkoff Peter McCrory Policy, Security, and Society Jack Clark Marina Favaro Jim Baker Projects in this workstream may include: Designing and conducting empirical research on AI's economic effects, drawing on external data sources Developing new methodological approaches for studying AI's impact on labor markets, the future of work, and society Analysing the offense–defense balance for AI-enabled cyber and bio capabilities as models scale Measuring the extent to which model performance increases with custom harnesses Identifying market driven mechanisms that could improve societal resilience to anticipated threats from AI systems Identifying which metrics relating to AI R&D could serve as early warning signals for recursive self-improvement For past project examples, see: How AI Impacts Skill Formation : Judy Shen and Alex Tamkin Stress-Testing Model Specs Reveals Character Differences among Language Models : Jifan Zhang, Henry Sleight, Andi Peng, John Schulman, and Esin Durmus Unique candidate criteria You might be a particularly great fit for this workstream if you: Have an interest in economics or policy research; prior experience in this area is a plus but not required Are adaptable and collaborative, able to take direction and contribute to team priorities rather than needing to pursue a predetermined research agenda Are skilled at writing up and communicating your results, even when they're null or unexpected Are passionate about translating research insights into actionable recommendations for improving AI systems and informing policy You may be a good fit if you: Are motivated by making sure AI is safe and beneficial for society as a whole Are excited to transition into AI research and would be interested in a full-time role at Anthropic Strong track record of empirical research Thrive in fast-paced, collaborative environments Can implement ideas quickly and communicate clearly Candidates must be: Fluent in Python programming Available to work full-time on the Fellows program Logistics - Fellows Program Submit your application to the Anthropic Institute Fellows at the bottom of this page. Logistics Requirements: To participate in the Fellows program, you must have work authorization in the US, UK, or Canada and be located in that country during the program. Workspace Locations: We have designated shared workspaces in SF. We are also open to remote fellows in the UK, US, or Canada . Visa Sponsorship: We are not currently able to sponsor visas for fellows. To participate in the Fellows program, you need to have or independently obtain full-time work authorization in the UK, the US, or Canada. Program Duration: The program runs for 4 months, full-time. If you can't commit to the full duration, please still apply and note your constraints in the application. We review these requests on a case-by-case basis. The below are Anthropic's policies for full time roles. These do NOT apply to the Fellows Program. Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.salary_text: target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $405,000 USD Logistics Minim
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. Commercial Associate, Data Center Asset Management About the role Anthropic leases large data center campuses from developers, and our compute roadmap depends on those campuses being built, energized and handed over on schedule. When a signed project slips, the fastest fix is often commercial: change who pays for what, who controls what, and what happens when a date is missed. This team renegotiates signed deals to get projects back on track and then makes sure what was agreed actually happens. You will be second chair on every one of those negotiations, working directly with the team lead, and we expect you to be able to run a site on your own within six to nine months. What you will do Run the issues list on live renegotiations and keep parallel papers conformed (term sheets with more than one counterparty, amendments, side letters, schedules), catching the differences before the other side does. Turn first drafts of term sheets, amendments and formal notices with in house and outside counsel. Write the internal approval memo and collect sign offs from Finance, Legal, Construction, Power and Operations. It means the microgrid layer that ties them together: islanding and resynchronization, black-start, load-shedding, and generation dispatch. When a transformer slips three weeks at the factory, a data hall slips three weeks at the site. We're hiring a Supply Chain Delivery Manager to own that equipment from purchase order to dock. You will be the site-facing supply chain lead for a regional portfolio of data center projects: tracking every OFE line item against the construction schedule, running factory and logistics escalations with OEMs, holding suppliers and general contractors accountable for delivery performance, and giving leadership a clear, converged picture of delivery risk across the portfolio. Your job is to make sure equipment production and delivery are never the reason a site misses its ready-for-service date. This is a senior individual-contributor role on the Compute DC Infrastructure team, working daily with Construction, Electrical and Mechanical Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, Commissioning, and our general contractors and OEMs. It is not a category-management or negotiation role — Sourcing owns supplier strategy and commercial terms — and it is not a people-management role. The emphasis is execution: schedules, escalations, logistics, and site readiness. What You'll Do Delivery planning and schedule integration Own the end-to-end OFE delivery plan for each site in your portfolio: order placement, engineering submittal/approval milestones, production slots, FAT dates, ship dates, and required-on-site (ROS) dates, integrated with the GC's construction schedule. Engage during preconstruction with Construction, Engineering, and the GC to set OFE delivery expectations, sequence equipment arrivals to the build, and identify schedule risk before POs are cut. Lead OFE kickoff meetings at the site level with the GC and internal construction teams, establishing points of contact, delivery windows, receiving requirements, and escalation paths. Maintain the single source of truth for OFE status across the portfolio — a live tracker of every line item, its milestone dates, and its risk rating. Supplier execution and escalation Run weekly delivery cadences with OEMs and integrators on open orders; verify production progress against committed slots rather than accepting reported dates at face value. Act as the primary escalation point for factory slips, component shortages, FAT failures, and shipping delays; drive recovery plans (expedites, partial ships, resequencing, alternate sources) with Sourcing and Engineering. Partner with Sourcing on corporate-level supplier escalations, bringing site-level schedule intelligence to commercial conversations. Hold GC OFCI teams accountable for receiving, storage, and installation-readiness performance; manage the change/claim process when delivery issues affect the GC's schedule. Logistics and site readiness Plan and coordinate transportation for oversize/overweight and high-value equipment — carrier selection, route surveys, permits, crane and rigging coordination — with our logistics partners and the GC. Manage laydown, staging, and interim storage decisions when site readiness and equipment arrival diverge; coordinate with Quality and Commissioning on receiving inspection and storage/preservation requirements. Ensure equipment arrives complete — accessories, spares, documentation, and vendor startup support scheduled — so installation and commissioning are not delayed by missing pieces. Risk management and reporting Identify, triage, and report delivery risks across the portfolio; propose solutions and drive decisions to protect capacity milestones. Establish and lead recurring Capacity Delivery Reviews giving leadership converged visibility into OFE delivery status and risk by site and by equipment category. Track delivery KPIs — on-time-to-ROS, schedule drift by supplier and category, escalation cycle time, expedite spend — and use them to surface systemic issues. Feed lessons learned back into Sourcing (lead-time assumptions, contract delivery terms, buffer strategy) and Construction (ROS sequencing) to improve the next program. You've managed cross-functional escalations across construction teams, suppliers, and internal partners, and you know when to expedite, when to resequence, and when to escalate commercially. Comfortable reading and influencing construction schedules (P6 or MS Project) and tying equipment milestones to them. Strong written and verbal communication — you can turn a messy delivery problem into a one-page recommendation for leadership. Data-fluent: you build and maintain trackers and dashboards, and you'd rather look at the numbers than trust a status email. By focusing on systemic change, AV is working to improve the lives of American families, strengthen their communities, and promote their economic opportunity. Position Overview AV’s Criminal Justice team advances evidence-based, cost-effective strategies to improve public safety and promote fairness. The team focuses on solving more crimes faster, improving prison rehabilitation, and advancing other high-impact policy opportunities through research, policy development, and advocacy. AV is seeking a Manager, Criminal Justice Policy to identify, analyze, develop, and pitch new, high-leverage grants opportunities aligned with our strategies; manage current philanthropic investments; engage a variety of stakeholders, both internal and external, in research, policy, and advocacy. This is a great opportunity for someone interested in learning more about criminal justice policy and the role of philanthropy in catalyzing evidence-based change. Managers gain exposure to a wide range of policy issues, build meaningful connections across the field, and develop a strong understanding of how philanthropic investments drive impact. This position will be based in our New York City or Washington, DC office and will report to the Vice President, Criminal Justice overseeing community safety work. Core Responsibilities • In collaboration with the Criminal Justice leadership team, help identify, assess, develop, and pitch high-impact policy and grant opportunities aligned with the team’s strategy, including solving more crimes faster, prison rehabilitation, and selective responsive work where AV can add value. • Manage grants and investments, track progress and implementation, assess impact, and draw lessons from grantees and partners to inform strategic priorities, future funding opportunities, and course corrections. • Provide thought partnership to prospective and current grantees on project design, deliverables, implementation plans, performance metrics, and opportunities to build or translate evidence for policy use. • Develop and manage relationships with policymakers, agency leaders, practitioners, researchers, advocates, experts, and new and existing grantees to support practical, evidence-based criminal justice policy solutions. • Analyze legislation, policy proposals, implementation models, and state or federal developments; draft clear summaries, recommendations, talking points, and other materials to support strategy and decision-making. • Help field, triage, track, and respond to requests from policymakers and AV’s advocacy team by identifying evidence, policy options, implementation considerations, evaluation opportunities, and appropriate internal or external partners. • Organize or support stakeholder convenings, briefings, and learning opportunities that advance the team’s goals, strengthen credibility with partners, and connect research, policy, advocacy, and implementation needs. • Travel to attend conferences, meet with grantees or partners, support state or federal policy work, or collaborate with colleagues in other AV offices, as needed. • Other duties to support the team’s work, as needed. In addition, a relocation bonus is available for candidates who will move to one of AV’s three office locations for a position. Candidates who have been impacted by the systems we are seeking to change are strongly encouraged to apply. jobs.title: Job Title Project Manager and Research Analyst (Job ID: 2026-3920)
jobs.description: Overview Join one of the most influential, most quoted, and most trusted think tanks! The Brookings Institution is a nonprofit public policy organization based in Washington, D.C. Our mission is to equip decision-makers with nonpartisan research and policy strategies to create a more prosperous and secure country and world. To advance our mission, we are committed to the following four goals: Develop economic growth strategies for a changing world Expand economic and social opportunity for all Revitalize U.S. democratic institutions Advance peace and security worldwide At the core of our mission is the quality, independence, and impact of our research. We are dedicated to finding bold, pragmatic solutions for societal challenges through open-minded inquiry, diverse perspectives, and holding ourselves to the highest standards of scholastic rigor. Beyond the pursuit of excellence and intellectual rigor, Brookings places immense value on creating a supportive and collaborative environment where every individual can do their best work, learn, and grow. Because of this, Brookings has been at the forefront of public policy for more than a century. The Global Economy and Development program at Brookings aims to shape the policy debate on how to improve global economic cooperation and fight global poverty and sources of social stress. The Workforce of the Future (WoF) initiative focuses on innovative policy solutions at the intersection of industrial policy, economic development, immigration policy, and the future of work. WoF is seeking a Project Manager and Research Analyst (PMRA) to work closely with the Senior Fellow advance the initiative’s research and policy agenda. This is a dynamic role that combines research, policy analysis, project management, writing, data analytics, and high-profile public engagement. Note: Please be advised that Brookings is currently undergoing a multi-year strategic implementation, and as part of this effort, your role, supervisor, and program may change. Position Location : This position is hybrid. Hybrid positions combine regular in-person presence at our Washington, DC office with the option of two days of remote work each week. Please note: This position is included in the staff bargaining unit, Brookings United, affiliated with the IFPTE Local 70 union, and is covered under the terms of the collective bargaining agreement. Responsibilities Ready to contribute to Brookings success? The PMRA will bring strong analytical and writing skills, critical thinking, sound judgement, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to manage complex projects and priorities independently. A flexible and entrepreneurial mindset will be essential, always with an eye toward opportunities for innovation and amplifying impact. Responsibilities will include conducting in-depth research and analysis; drafting policy memos, presentations, and other written products; managing complex projects and partnerships; supporting high-profile public engagements and convenings; and serving as a key point of contact for internal and external stakeholders. The PMRA will have the opportunity to engage across a range of policy issues and work closely with researchers, policymakers, and other leaders in the field. Preference will be given to candidates with expertise in one or more of the following areas: regional economic development; labor economics and workforce policy; AI and its effects on the workforce; and data visualization and interactive tools. This is a one-year termed position with extension dependent on funding. 50% Project Management Supports the Senior Fellow and Assistant Research Director in day-to-day project management tasks. Closely monitors and adjusts project timelines and work plans, communicates upcoming deadlines and priorities, and works closely with the Senior Fellow and other relevant team members to ensure smooth, on-schedule implementation of project activities. Assists the Senior Fellow by providing administrative and coordination support, including meeting scheduling. Provides primary support and coordinates the planning, execution, and follow-up related to roundtables, workshops and events with high-profile stakeholders. Drafts speeches, testimony and memos on substantive topics for review by the Senior Fellow and project team. Generate impactful communications material and social media strategy to disseminate research and coordinates engagement with external media. Coordinates with internal colleagues from finance, development, and communications departments. Represents the project at relevant public events and meetings. Other administrative duties as assigned. 50% Research and Policy Analysis Conduct research and policy analysis on topics including workforce, industrial policy, international development and immigration. Perform quantitative data analysis using large data sets. Create tables, graphs, and other data visualizations that clearly communicate research findings. Support the research team in the writing of high-quality drafts of working papers and presentations based on the research. Conduct literature reviews, monitor and analyze relevant material from topical conferences, academic journals, and policy publications. Support Senior Fellow with drafting, editing, and proof reading of research reports, policy briefs, blogs, online visualizations and other published materials. Other research assistance duties as assigned. Qualifications Ready to make an impact? In this role, you will support Brookings values of collegiality, respect, inclusion, diversity and community, and bring the following qualifications: Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in economics, political science, sociology or related social science field required. Master’s degree preferred. Strong academic record. Minimum of four years of relevant professional experience spanning research, project management, policy analysis, or related work. Excellent writing and communications skills. Familiarity with key sources of economic data and core scholarship on industrial policy, migration, labor, or social policy. Data visualization and editorial experience, a plus. Demonstrated experience engaging policymakers. jobs.description: ABOUT THE CAMPAIGN FINANCE BOARD   The Campaign Finance Board is a nonpartisan, independent city agency that empowers New Yorkers to have a greater impact on their elections. Our mission is to make local democracy more open, transparent, and equitable by removing barriers to participation.  We make it easier for New Yorkers to vote, meaningfully support candidates for city office, and run for office themselves. NYC Votes, our voter engagement initiative, meets people where they are to share trustworthy election information and help New Yorkers make a plan to vote. We publish the citywide Voter Guide, which delivers information about candidates directly to voters’ doors. Our public matching funds program ensures small contributions can make a big difference, allowing regular people to run for office by relying on the support of other regular people, not just wealthy donors and special interests. And we lift the veil on how candidates raise and spend money, increasing transparency and accountability in local government.   We believe that when every New Yorker is empowered to participate meaningfully in elections, candidates will better reflect the communities they serve, elected leaders will be more accountable to the public, and New Yorkers will have a democracy they can truly trust.   ABOUT THE UNIT  PUBLIC AFFAIRS DIVISION   The Public Affairs division engages New Yorkers, informs them about elections, and boosts their participation in the democratic process. We make election information accessible and relevant, increase engagement with underrepresented communities, and cultivate a team that reflects our core values of purpose, curiosity, creativity, and collaboration.    The division includes Marketing and Digital Communications, Community Engagement, Language Access, and Public Relations. Our division’s work includes publishing the citywide Voter Guide, running the official citywide Debates Program, and managing the voter engagement initiative, NYC Votes.  PUBLIC RELATIONS UNIT   The Public Relations unit leads messaging and strategy for internal and external communications and oversees the citywide Debates program as well as Board meetings and other events. The team works with journalists to land and shape coverage of campaign finance and election matters, and it works to strengthen communications inside the agency through collaboration with other units on the rollout of internal policies, identifying new ways to share and present internal updates, and creating new channels for engagement and building shared understanding of our work and mission.   JOB DESCRIPTION   The Events Coordinator will report to the Events Manager in the Public Relations Unit and will be responsible for driving logistics in the planning, coordination, and execution of internal and external CFB events including official monthly Campaign Finance Board meetings, staff meetings, and the official NYC Debates Program in years with an election for citywide office.   The Public Affairs division and Public Relations unit are dynamic and talented teams; this role offers growth potential and opportunities to learn about all facets of our work, including the city’s public matching funds program, the NYC Votes initiative to engage communities underserved by electoral outreach and local democracy, and policy recommendations to make New York City’s government more open, equitable, and transparent.    The person in this role will work closely with the Public Relations team, other Public Affairs division staff, and external stakeholders to ensure CFB events reflect the highest agency and industry standards. The ideal candidate will enjoy working collaboratively, effectively manage multiple workstreams at once, and believe in the mission of strengthening democracy in New York City.    The responsibilities and tasks to be completed in this role include, but are not limited to:    -  Support in the planning and execution of CFB hosted events -- for both internal staff and external attendees -- at external venues outside of the CFB office.      -  Coordinating virtual and hybrid event logistics to ensure live streaming, Q&A functions, accessibility support including American Sign Language (ASL) and language interpretation services, archival recordings, and other elements are executed seamlessly.     -  Providing training and prep materials for participants in CFB events such as runs-of-show executed to the highest degree of detail and professionalism.     -  Collaborating across the Public Affairs division to expand agency-wide best practices for engaging, inclusive, accessible events that further our mission.   MOST ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES & OTHER BEHAVIORS (KSAOs)   We're seeking individuals eager to make an impact, even if they don't tick every box on our job description.
