jobs.title: Evaluation Coordinator, Sexual and Reproductive Health and Equity Unit, Bureau of Maternal Infant and Reproductive Health
jobs.description: Since its creation as the Board of Health in 1805, DOHMH has set the national standard for public health. DOHMH has been a leader in utilizing community-level survey and epidemiologic data, cutting-edge information technology, and evidence-based and evidence-informed practices to prioritize and address the health issues of ultimate importance to NYC’s 8.4 million residents. DOHMH balances its role of protecting and promoting the health of all New Yorkers with the rights of those individuals to determine their own health-related behaviors. It achieves this balance by investing in public health interventions that work with communities to change the environmental context, making healthy options the default choice, regardless of education, income, and socioeconomic status. Within DOHMH, the Division of Family and Child Health (FCH) works to improve the health of children, women, and families in New York City, with an emphasis on reducing health disparities and advancing equity. The Division’s diverse and expansive portfolio of work ranges from providing home visits to new parents, to caring for acute and chronic conditions in school children, to engaging communities around promoting sexual and reproductive justice. Four bureaus comprise the Division: Bureau of Maternal, Infant and Reproductive Health, Bureau of Early Intervention, Office of School Health, and Bureau of Administration. We encourage qualified applicants with demonstrated commitment to social justice, particularly racial, gender, and LGBTQ equity to apply.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Support SRHE Unit evaluation activities by providing technical, administrative, and research support for all aspects of the evaluation • Manage all data collection and research efforts, including: o Overseeing data entry o Providing assistance in developing and implementing data collection tools o Designing and maintaining databases using Microsoft Excel, Salesforce, and the performance measures platform provided by the funder o Cleaning, manipulating, and analyzing data using various statistical software packages such as SAS and R o Demonstrating familiarity with geocoding techniques o Preparing IRB applications, as needed • Liaise and work closely with schools, community and school-based clinics, and other implementation partners to facilitate data collection efforts • Assist with the preparation of periodic written reports to monitor the progress of all evaluation objectives, as well as generate manuscripts and presentations • Conduct literature reviews, as needed • Remain current on the latest data, trends, and best practices in adolescent sexual and reproductive health • Present and disseminate data on behalf of the unit at conferences, meetings, and other venues • Fulfill various data requests for program and other internal agency staff • Assist with other duties, tasks, and special projects as may be required by the NYCDOHMH  PREFERRED SKILLS: • Academic training in epidemiology (MPH or MS), with an emphasis on sexual and reproductive health • Strong quantitative analytic skills (qualitative skills are desired) • Ability to manipulate and analyze data using statistical software such as SAS and R • Strong organizational skills with good follow-through to complete assignments within specified timeframe • Strong written, verbal and editing skills, including summaries, reports, manuscripts, and presentations • Proficient in Microsoft Office, Tableau, and ArcGIS  Why you should work for us:  - jobs.title: Evaluation Specialist, Bureau of Hepatitis, HIV, and STI
jobs.description: The Division of Disease Control’s mission is to safeguard the health of New Yorkers through identification, surveillance, treatment, control, and prevention of infectious diseases, which is achieved through varied and interrelated endeavors of its seven Bureaus. The Bureau of Hepatitis, HIV, and Sexually Transmitted Infections’ (BHHS) mission is to improve the lives of New Yorkers by ending transmission, illness, stigma, and inequities related to viral hepatitis, HIV, and sexually transmitted infections. BHHS accomplishes its mission through testing initiatives; prevention, care, and treatment programming ;epidemiology and surveillance; training and technical assistance; community engagement; social marketing; policy advocacy; and racial equity and social justice initiatives. BHHS's HIV Care and Treatment Program(CTP) is the Recipient of the Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program(RWHAP) Part A grant, the RWHAP Ending the HIV Epidemic(EHE)cooperative agreement, and the Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS (HOPWA) grant. CTP consists of six units: 1) Quality Management & Program Implementation, 2) Program Planning & Compliance, 3) EHE Initiative Services, 4) Housing Services, 5) Special Projects & Initiatives, and 6) Research and Evaluation.   Working closely with other Evaluation Specialists, Data Analysts, and Senior Research Analysts, the Evaluation Specialist (Civil Service Title: City Research Scientist II) in the Research and Evaluation Unit will contribute to evaluation and reporting for RWHAP (Part A and EHE) programs and assist on other projects as needed. This opening offers a rare opportunity to join a stellar team in advancing health practice, policy, and science through the effective use and communication of data.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Providing specifications, testing, documentation, and provider/user support and materials on data systems, including the Electronic System for HIV Reporting and Evaluation (eSHARE). • Developing data collection tools and/or analytic methods to identify populations of focus, inform quality management/ improvement, assess program outcomes, and reduce health disparities. • Cleaning, managing, analyzing, and displaying data using analytic software packages (primarily SAS). • Reviewing syntax/code and supervising task completion for analyses by other REU staff. • Interpreting and disseminating findings through reports, presentations, and papers for publication. • Developing and managing multiple research/evaluation projects. • Participating in core unit activities, including responding to data requests and coordinating the matching of records across data sources. • Supporting federal grant deliverables and the local public health response to emergencies.  PREFERRED SKILLS: • Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills. • Knowledge of SAS (programming and analysis), Tableau (data visualization),and Adobe Acrobat, as well as Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and other MS Office software. • Experience with analyzing large health services program datasets and/or surveillance datasets. • An appreciation for data quality and program quality management. • Capacity to maintain multiple projects simultaneously, maintain productivity under pressure, and function effectively both independently and as part of a team. • Knowledge of HIV prevention and treatment, populations most affected by HIV, key HIV outcome measures, and structural determinants of health outcomes. • Effective translation of scientific information to facilitate its application in policy and practice. • Ability to work effectively with a diverse staff of scientists, IT specialists, planners, clinicians, program managers, and service providers within the NYC Health Department and at external agencies, as well as clients/consumers who participate in community planning and research review processes. jobs.title: Health Product Development & Engineering Lead, Bureau of Data Technology & Strategy
jobs.description: The Center for Population Health Data Science (CPHDS)- launched in October of 2023- aims to catalyze critical data modernization work and enable the agency to make progress toward linking public health, healthcare, and social service for timely and effective publication. We are working towards making these data more accessible, timely, equitable, meaningfully usable, and protected – and actively used to protect and promote the health and wellbeing of New Yorkers. We aim to strengthen agencywide data capabilities by empowering our workforce, enhancing intra- and inter-agency data sharing, and using modern technology to yield trusted and integrated data and insights. A real-time and comprehensive view of city needs is needed to enhance public health actions and improve health outcomes for the most vulnerable New Yorkers. The CPHDS is working to strengthen citywide population health surveillance by better linking public health, healthcare, and social service data to fully characterize and improve the health of New Yorkers. Our vision is for these data to be accessible, timely, equitable, meaningfully usable, and protected in order to protect and promote health and wellbeing of New Yorkers. The Bureau of Data Technology and Strategy (DTS) is home to data strategy, data communication, data governance, data product management, data engineering, and data science capabilities. The Unified Data Experience (UDX) team is working to modernize how the agency communicates data to the public, ensuring usability, accessibility, and approachability of al public-facing data communication products.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Lead the engineering and development of the UDX platform: choosing technologies, architectures, and componentry to support development and desired workflows. • Collaborate with team on research and design – turning internal and external needs into prototypes and prototypes into product. • Identify design or technical problems and devise elegant, timely, and cost-effective solutions. • Lead and guide other contributors including junior developers and UX designers. • Communicate design, development, and technical decisions and trade-o fs to internal stakeholders. • Ask insightful questions, take risks, and champion innovative ideas that facilitate the use of data for action.  PREFERRED SKILLS: • Four or more years of demonstrated leadership experience developing internally- and externally-facing data communication products like dashboards and web products. Preference will be given to candidates who have experience designing complex solutions and are enthusiastic about data visualization and data communication products. • Experience in accessible front-end web design using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, including familiarity with a wide range of contemporary web development tools and technologies, especially JavaScript-based open-source frameworks like React and Next.js. • A strong grasp of user-centered design principles or design thinking. • Experience with public health principles, health literacy, evidence-based health communications, or evidence-based data visualization techniques. • Familiarity with experimental thinking and ability to conduct A/B tests to determine best approaches. • Ability to work effectively in a team se ting including synthesizing abstract ideas into concrete designs. • Be passionate about resolving user pain points through great design. • Be open to receiving feedback and constructive criticism. jobs.title: Naloxone Informatics Specialist, Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use
jobs.description: The Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use Prevention, Care, and Treatment (BADUPCT) works to close gaps and reduce overall morbidity and mortality related to alcohol and substance use among New Yorkers. BADUPCT develops, implements, and evaluates interventions and prevention strategies through contracting of treatment, recovery and support services; policy analysis and development; epidemiology and surveillance; dissemination of treatment and management guidelines; harm reduction initiatives; public and provider outreach and education; and community involvement and interagency collaboration. The Bureau amplifies the voices of those most impacted and focuses on inequitable structural, social, service, and communication factors that drive disparities.  The Overdose Education and Naloxone Distribution Unit (OENDU) develops, implements, and evaluates initiatives to reduce and prevent opioid overdose deaths in New York City. The Unit provides naloxone, training, and technical assistance to over 350 Opioid Overdose Prevention Programs (OOPPs) across New York City. OOPPs provide community-based overdose prevention, recognition, and response education and distribute naloxone directly to community members. OENDU solicits data from these OOPPs to evaluate their naloxone dispensing. DOHMH has its own OOPP and provides in-person and virtual overdose prevention training and naloxone via mail-based distribution. In addition, OENDU provides contract management, fiscal, technical, and programmatic support to at least 27 contracted OOPPs for strategic naloxone distribution and 4 contracted OOPPs for the implementation and management of 8 Public Health Vending Machines.   Position Summary:    The Naloxone Informatics Specialist will support the Overdose Prevention Unit by supporting the submission of accurate and timely naloxone distribution data, with the goal of preventing overdose deaths in New York City.  Under general direction from the Naloxone Data Coordinator, with wide latitude for independent judgment and initiative, the Naloxone Informatics Specialist will:  Job Duties and Responsibilities:    •	Collaborate with colleagues in OENDU and the Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use (BADU) to gather and analyze data related to naloxone dispensing and distribution in NYC  •	Use Microsoft Access and/or R studio to clean and maintain data related to naloxone dispensing and distribution initiatives in NYC  •	Generate PowerBI dashboards and data tables to support the ongoing evaluation of naloxone dispensing and distribution initiatives in NYC.  •	Solicit monthly naloxone distribution reports from over 190 Opioid Overdose Prevention Programs (OOPPs); follow up with OOPPs who do not submit timely reports and provide technical assistance as needed  •	Train newly registered OOPPs to submit individual-level dispensing data through the Naloxone Dispensing Form (NDF); support OOPPs as they integrate form submission into their workflows; monitor form submission and provide support to OOPPs to increase their response rate.   •	Manage timely entry of monthly distribution reports into database; reconcile naloxone fulfillment with monthly data; manage timely preparation of report materials for data processing  •	Develop and refine surveys, RedCap forms, and other dispensing data collection forms as needed.  •	Collaborate with NYS Department of Health AIDS Institute, the Overdose Prevention Coordinator, the Naloxone Inventory Coordinator, and other BADUPCT staff to maintain registration and contact information for all OOPPs  •	Provide timely response to requests for naloxone fulfillment and dispensing data, naloxone reversals and other relevant information  •	Refine systems, as needed, for tracking naloxone dispensing data   •	Support Naloxone Inventory Coordinator in the packaging of naloxone kits  •	Participate in Overdose Prevention Unit meetings, including facilitation on a rotating basis; provide administrative support to the Overdose Prevention Unit including scheduling meetings, developing agendas, and other tasks as needed.  •	Participate in agency-wide activities for advancing racial, gender, and social equity.  •	Other duties or tasks may be assigned on an as-needed basis  Preferred Skills:   •	Knowledge of substance use issues and harm reduction practice and theory, including syringe exchange, overdose prevention and education for HIV and Hepatitis C prevention. •	Experience with quantitative data, including the ability to read, interpret and synthesize epidemiologic and other scientific literature. •	Ability to work independently and as part of a team. Possess exceptional interpersonal, research, written and verbal communication skills.  •	The candidate will also be detail-oriented with outstanding organizational skills.  •	Ability to multi-task in a fast-paced, high volume environment.  •	Proficiency in Excel, Access, Word, and PowerPoint. •	Experience querying or managing data using code, such as SQL, SAS, or R. jobs.title: One Health Analyst, Bureau of Communicable Diseases
jobs.description: The Bureau of Communicable Diseases (BCD), part of the Division of Disease Control, is responsible for the surveillance, prevention, and control of over 70 infectious diseases including foodborne, enteric, waterborne, respiratory, zoonotic and vector-borne diseases. You will assist the Antimicrobial Resistance Unit and the One Health team by providing dedicated analytical support to monitor and control multi drug resistant organisms in humans and animals in New York City. Within BCD, the Antimicrobial Resistance Unit (ARU) aims to 1) conduct surveillance for and facilitate rapid response to high-priority multidrug-resistant organisms, 2) undertake epidemiologic research on the transmission of these organisms in the community, and 3) promote judicious antibiotic prescribing practices and infection prevention efforts by disseminating resources to NYC stakeholders, including data on local antibiotic use and resistance trends. The ARU is comprised of three teams: the Surveillance and Data team, the Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) and Antimicrobial Stewardship (AS) team, and the One Health team. The goals of the One Health team are to understand and control the spread of multidrug-resistant organisms in humans, animals, and our shared environment.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: Under the supervision of the One Health team lead, this analyst will provide data support for both the One Health team specifically as well as the ARU more broadly. Their duties will include, but are not limited to:  • Building, maintaining, and strengthening surveillance of antimicrobial resistance and antimicrobial use data from humans and animals.  • Supporting IPC and AS for veterinary professionals including creating new and innovative resources. • Providing analytical support for whole genome sequencing (WGS) initiatives, including: o Coordinating with epidemiology, laboratory, informatics, and information technology teams to ensure proper transmission of WGS data.  o Developing and maintaining routine reports to analyze and share WGS data. • Providing analytical support for ARU projects including:  o Surveillance of carbapenem-resistant organisms (CRO) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in New York City and detection of community-associated transmission  o Core ARU duties and data needs such as CRO case investigations, routine data cleaning, quality assurance activities, etc. • Supporting project management needs based on data analytics.  • Presenting results of data analyses to internal and external stakeholders.  PREFERRED SKILLS: • Proficiency in Statistical Analysis Software (SAS), R, SQL, and/or REDCap • Proficiency in navigating computer systems; ability to learn new data systems quickly; and ability to comply with data integrity and security safeguards for personal identifiable information • Experience and training in public health, one health, and/or antimicrobial resistance • Excellent interpersonal skills including the ability to interact professionally with people from diverse cultural, racial, ethnic, gender, and socioeconomic backgrounds • A positive attitude and strong work ethic • Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, critical thinking ability, and sound judgment • Ability to speak, read, and write in English • Must be a NYC resident or become one within 90 days of hire  Why you should work for us:  - Loan Forgiveness: As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal/state loan forgiveness and repayment assistance programs that lessen your payments or even fully forgive your full balance. jobs.title: Program Analyst, Bureau of Hepatitis, HIV, and STI
jobs.description: The NYC Health Department’s Bureau of Hepatitis, HIV, and Sexually Transmitted Infections (BHHS), within the Division of Disease Control, oversees the City's response to viral hepatitis, HIV, and sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Its mission is to improve the lives of New Yorkers by ending transmission, illness, stigma, and inequities related to viral hepatitis, HIV, and STIs. BHHS does this through testing initiatives; prevention, care, and treatment programming; epidemiology and surveillance; training and technical assistance; community engagement; social marketing; policy advocacy; and racial equity and social justice initiatives. BHHS’s over 500 staff members work across eight programs: Administration, HIV Care and Treatment, HIV Epidemiology, HIV Prevention, Policy and External Affairs, Racial Equity and Social Justice Initiatives, STI, and Viral Hepatitis.   BHHS seeks an experienced epidemiologist and data analyst for its STI Program. The Program Analyst will work closely with and report directly to the Executive Director of the STI Program, but will provide administrative and technical support to leadership of all four STI units: Epidemiology, Research, and Evaluation; Program Development and Implementation; Surveillance; and Case Investigations and Partner Services. We are seeking a reliable and conscientious team member to join our dedicated and collaborative staff. The Bureau of Division Management & Systems Coordination (DMSC) leads administrative, surveillance, informatics, preparedness, policy, communications, community engagement, and racial equity and social justice activities for the Division and guides the strategic use of Division resources to advance innovative and effective policies and programs.   We are seeking to fill a position in the Division of Disease Control that will provide key support for grant coordination and sustainability initiatives. It is expected that the position will work 35 hours per week to help coordinate grant related activities, track progress on grant milestones, support cross-bureau programmatic coordination, and assist with sustainability initiatives and other projects. This position will work across teams and bureaus to ensure timely reporting and alignment with organizational goals and will report to the Director, Programs and Strategy within DMSC. jobs.title: Program Manager, Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention
jobs.description: The Center for Health Equity & Community Wellness (CHECW) seeks to eliminate racial and other inequities resulting in premature mortality.  With an unwavering grounding in history and structural analysis, CHECW works to increase visibility of the harm perpetuated by centuries of racist, socially unjust policy while pushing towards redress for the most impacted NYC communities. CHECW addresses inequity across community and healthcare systems in partnership with community, faith-based, and health care organizations. CHECW's work focuses on social determinants of health, including environmental and commercial determinants, and addresses both upstream and downstream factors to improve health and well-being of New Yorker. CHECW is comprised of the Bureau of Bronx Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Brooklyn Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Harlem Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Queens Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention, the Bureau of Equitable Health Systems and the Bureau of Finance, Administration and Services. The division's Deputy Commissioner also serves as the Agency's Chief Equity Officer and oversees Race To Justice, the Agency's internal reform effort to help our staff learn what they can do to better address racial health gaps and improve health outcomes for all New Yorkers. The NYC Health Department's Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention (BDCP) strives to reduce the burden of chronic disease, including heart disease, diabetes, and cancer, among New Yorkers. BCDP focuses on nutrition, tobacco use, the built environment, and reducing the impact of cancer. BCDP aims to advance evidence-based policies, programs, community engagement, and research aimed at shifting environments, changing systems and promoting health equity. As a bureau within the NYC Health Department's Center for Health Equity & Community Wellness (CHECW), BCDP contributes to CHECW's goal of eliminating racial inequities and reducing overall premature mortality among New Yorkers. BCDP puts a focus on reducing exposure to and consumption of unhealthy foods and tobacco industry products and countering industry practices that negatively impact health. In addition to pursuing population-level approaches, BCDP prioritizes communities that bear a disproportionate burden of chronic disease.   The Active Design Unit within BCDP seeks to hire a Program Manager, the Program Manager will oversee the implementation and day to day management of the unit's place-based programs in schools and neighborhood settings, including program planning, partnership coordination, research, and evaluation activities.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Oversee and implement place-based program projects that advance the goals of the Active Design Unit and BCDP, in close collaboration with community-based organizations, government agencies, consultants, and other external partners.  • In collaboration with unit Director, manage and oversee programmatic budgets, contracts, and procurement.  • Manage strategic relationships with peer city agencies, community organizations, academic institutions, and other external partners to share information, coordinate activities, and collaborate on projects that support and inform the work of the Active Design Unit.  • Support community engagement and partner coordination throughout program planning and implementation, including activities that incorporate community perspectives and lived experience into Active Design projects.  • Prepare program updates, grant proposals, funder progress reports, and other written materials to communicate program activities, accomplishments, and outcomes.  • Supervise and manage staff and other team members as assigned, providing guidance, setting priorities, and overseeing work assignments.  • Conduct research and review public health and built environment literature to inform the design and implementation of evidence-informed initiatives that leverage urban planning, architecture, and design strategies to promote healthy behaviors and improve health outcomes.  • Coordinate with Bureau and agency colleagues and external city agency and private partners to plan and implement research and evaluation activities in support of Active Design programs and strategic initiatives.  • Support the development and implementation of data collection and evaluation protocols to document program implementation, participation, utilization, and outcomes, and contribute to analyses, reports, presentations, and peer-reviewed publications. • Monitor and synthesize emerging research, best practices, and public policy developments related to the built environment, physical activity, mental health, social connection, and other health outcomes, particularly in school and neighborhood se tings.  • Plan and coordinate meetings and events, including developing event logistics, preparing presentations and other materials, and communicating program information to key audiences.  • Contribute to the development of reports, publications, presentations, and other knowledge-sharing materials that communicate best practices and practical strategies for integrating Active Design into school and neighborhood settings.  • Perform additional duties as needed.  PREFERRED SKILLS: • Three years of full-time experience in program management, community-based programming, public health, government, or a related field. • Knowledge of chronic disease prevention, physical activity, the built environment, and/or Active Design. • Excellent oral, written, organizational, and interpersonal communication skills. • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities, work collaboratively across disciplines, and build effective relationships with diverse stakeholders. • Strong project management and coordination skills, including the ability to work effectively with government agencies, community organizations, consultants, academic partners, and other external stakeholders. • Willingness to travel throughout NYC  Why you should work for us:  - Loan Forgiveness: As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal/state loan forgiveness and repayment assistance programs that lessen your payments or even fully forgive your full balance. jobs.title: Program Manager, Bureau of Tuberculosis Control
jobs.description: The mission of the Bureau of Tuberculosis Control (BTBC) is to prevent the spread of tuberculosis (TB) and eliminate it as a public health problem in New York City. The office of Medical Affairs is looking to fil the role of Program Manager. The Program Manager will provide programmatic leadership across multiple non-clinical functions within the Office of Medical Affairs, overseeing program operations, supervising professional staff, and leading program improvement and evaluation initiatives. The group includes non-clinical staff working in areas including drug-resistant TB case management, regulatory affairs, and the evaluation of newly arrived immigrants and refugees at risk for TB disease. The Program Manager will oversee a portfolio of activities in these areas and supervise professional staff with specialized program responsibilities.   The ideal candidate will be an experienced public health professional with strong leadership, program management, and analytical skills. They will use data to assess program performance and identify opportunities for improvement and will demonstrate initiative, sound judgment, and the ability to translate complex programmatic challenges into actionable solutions.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Use surveillance, clinical, and operational data to monitor program performance, identify gaps and trends, evaluate interventions, and inform program and policy decisions. • Lead or contribute to research and evaluation activities, including study design and data analysis; protocols and IRB submissions; and preparation of reports, presentations, abstracts, and manuscripts. • Provide leadership and oversight for assigned program areas, including program implementation, performance monitoring, operational improvement, and continuity of essential functions. • Supervise and mentor professional staff, establish priorities, oversee work assignments, provide feedback, and support staff development and increasing independence. • Identify programmatic challenges and opportunities for improvement and independently develop, implement, and evaluate solutions. • Lead public health projects and initiatives from planning through implementation and evaluation, collaborating with clinical, epidemiologic, analytical, and operational staff and external partners as needed. • Develop and improve program protocols, workflows, policies, and standard operating procedures, including cross-training and coverage plans to strengthen program continuity. jobs.title: Program Manager, Developmental Disabilities, Bureau of Children, Youth, Families & Developmental Disabilities
jobs.description: The Bureau of Children, Youth, Families & Developmental Disabilities (CYF-DD) is responsible for planning and monitoring much of NYC's comprehensive network of child and adolescent community mental health services. CYF-DD relies on research and surveillance to guide its decisions around service planning, implementation and evaluation and incorporates a health equity lens into its work. CYF-DD oversees a portfolio of over 100 programs and supports a family-driven, individualized and strength-based approach to care. The portfolio includes a range of programs for children and adults with intellectual or developmental disabilities (I/DD), including (a) recreational; (b) clinical; and (c) vocational programs.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: - Lead a strategic planning process to identify (a) need for programs that serve individuals with co-occurring I/DD and MH conditions, (b) current programs available to these individuals and (c) gaps that need to be addressed. - Assess local, state, and national best practices relating to services for individuals with co-occurring I/DD and mental health conditions. - Design new program models for individuals with co-occurring I/DD and mental health conditions, informed by evidence-based practices. - Mobilize additional resources through development of new needs requests and grant proposals - Lead the procurement and process to select vendors that provide services for individuals with I/DD - Support the development of referral pathways to improve access to I/DD services. - Collaborate with the bureau policy team to identify and analyze policy issues and develop policy recommendations. - Work closely with Data and Program Quality Analysts in the Bureau to identify meaningful metrics for the I/DD portfolio of programs and develop a data reporting process. - Supervise Specialist Consultant(s) to manage the overall I/DD portfolio of programs which includes: ensuring program adherence to scopes, budgets, and regulations through site visits and data analysis; overseeing corrective action plans to improve performance, if needed; and liaising with appropriate DOHMH staff to resolve budgetary or contractual matters. - Provide subject matter expertise to staff in the Bureau, Division and Agency - Guide and/or provide technical assistance to contracted providers to ensure program quality and effectiveness and equity - Oversee mental health data reporting from provider agencies and use it to inform continuous quality improvement. - Review, synthesize, and report data findings, providing actionable recommendations for the Bureau’s portfolio of IDD programs. - Act as key liaison to OPWDD, NYC Health & Hospitals, and Divisions in OMH that focus on co-occurring conditions. - Foster strong relationships with internal DOHMH programs, other City agencies and State agencies as well as provider agencies that provide I/DD services. - Convene and facilitate stakeholder meetings, through agenda preparation and follow-up on action items. - Collaborate with the Office of Policy and Planning on systems planning and stakeholder engagement. - Supervise one or more program consultants  PREFERRED SKILLS: - Extensive experience working with the I/DD service system, community-based mental health programs, public health initiatives, or behavioral health integration. - Ability to build partnerships and collaborate with government agencies, healthcare providers, and community-based organizations. - Experience incorporating racial equity and social justice principles into program operations and a demonstrated commitment to supporting communities affected by systemic oppression and bias. - Strong teamwork and collaboration skills, with the ability to function effectively both independently and as part of a multi-stakeholder team. jobs.title: Program Quality Manager, Bureau of Hepatitis, HIV, and STI
jobs.description: The NYC Health Department’s Bureau of Hepatitis, HIV, and Sexually Transmitted Infections (BHHS) falls within the Division of Disease Control, oversees the City's response to viral hepatitis, HIV, and sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Its mission is to improve the lives of New Yorkers by ending transmission, illness, stigma, and inequities related to viral hepatitis, HIV, and STIs. BHHS does this through testing initiatives; prevention, care, and treatment programming; epidemiology and surveillance; training and technical assistance; community engagement; social marketing; policy advocacy; and racial equity and social justice initiatives. BHHS’s over 500 staff members work across eight programs: Administration, HIV Care and Treatment, HIV Epidemiology, HIV Prevention, Policy and External Affairs, Racial Equity and Social Justice Initiatives, STI, and Viral Hepatitis. The Viral Hepatitis Program conducts surveillance, and develops and implements programs and projects to prevent, manage and treat hepatitis B and C in New York City.   Reporting to the Project Director and working with the Capacity Building unit, you will be assigned specific viral hepatitis linkage to care initiatives and strategies addressing the Plan to Eliminate Viral Hepatitis in New York City by 2030. Under direction of the Project Director and Director of Capacity Building, you will develop, implement, and evaluate program activities; meeting with external organization staff (such as program managers, clinicians, and service providers) to understand their program implementation and service delivery needs; and provide tailored technical assistance to support effective program outcomes.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Monitor contracts and budgets ensuring timely and accurate invoicing in compliance with agency policies and procedures. • Plan and coordinate with contractors the implementation of linkage to care initiatives program model and evidence-based practices (using Salesforce, MS Teams and Planner. • Analyze program data and conduct quality assurance (using REDCap, SAS, Tableau, MS Forms). • Engage collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders to address service delivery needs and improve program outcomes. • Develop, implement and evaluate quality improvement projects to increase viral hepatitis screening, linkage to care, and treatment rates. • Conduct comprehensive literature reviews and critically evaluate health research studies to support implementation of evidence-based strategies and interventions. • Stay up to date on the latest trends, developments and innovations related to viral hepatitis screening, linkage to care, treatment and relevant topics such as immigration and substance use to enhance overall effectiveness of the program. • Contribute to the development and dissemination of program protocols, resources and tools to support program outcomes. • Maintain accurate records and prepare reports. • Support the dissemination of program findings, including for presentations and manuscripts. • Supervise one or two staff. • Contribute to Capacity Building and Viral Hepatitis Program activities. • Contribute to the Bureau’s racial justice and health equity activities. • Complete other tasks as assigned.  PREFERRED SKILLS: • Master’s degree from an accredited college or university with a specialization in public health, health management, or a related field • Strong working knowledge of Salesforce, REDCap SAS, Tableau, Excel and other MS Office software • Experience and expertise in collecting, managing, cleaning, analyzing, and reporting data • Experience in project management, including planning, implementation, and evaluation activities • Ability to coordinate, engage, and foster collaboration among diverse stakeholders, including community organizations, and health care providers • Knowledge of implementation science and public health interventions • Strong written and oral communication skills • Ability to work both independently and within a team • Adaptability and willingness to learn • Ability to prioritize and manage multiple tasks • Professionalism and reliability • Initiative and proactive approach to work • Knowledge of hepatitis B and C, including prevention, control strategies, and current epidemiological trends, as well as broader infectious disease expertise (preferred but not required). jobs.title: Project Coordinator- Contracts, Bureau of the Public Health laboratory
jobs.description: The New York City (NYC) Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) is a public health leader serving over 8.4 million New York City residents from diverse ethnic, cultural, and economic backgrounds. The NYC Public Health Laboratory (PHL) is one of the largest local public health laboratories in the United States offering a dynamic and innovative work environment where employees contribute to the health and safety of NYC residents by providing clinical and environmental laboratory testing services. With more than 100 years of leadership in public health, a team of over 200 scientific and support staff that are committed to its mission to safeguard the health of all NYC residents by providing quality laboratory testing services that support the priorities of the NYC DOHMH and its community partners to prevent and respond to clinical and environmental public health concerns.   The New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (NYCDOHMH), Bureau of Public Health Laboratory is seeking to hire a Project Coordinator- Contracts. jobs.title: Qualitative Research Analyst, Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use
jobs.description: The Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use (BADU) works to close gaps and reduce overall morbidity and mortality related to alcohol and substance use among New Yorkers. BADU develops, implements, and evaluates interventions and prevention strategies through contracting of treatment, recovery and support services; policy analysis and development; epidemiology and surveillance; dissemination of treatment and management guidelines; harm reduction initiatives; public and provider outreach and education; and community involvement and interagency collaboration. The Bureau amplifies the voices of those most impacted and focuses on inequitable structural, social, service, and communication factors that drive disparities. The Office of Research, Surveillance, Policy, and Communications within BADU conducts alcohol- and drug-related surveillance, program evaluation and research, maintains databases, designs research protocols, produces reports, writes scientific articles for peer-reviewed journals, facilitates program and policy development, and develops messaging and other communication materials for provider and public audiences.   The Qualitative Research Analyst will support the development and implementation of BADU’s qualitative research and evaluation activities, including project design, data collection, analysis, and dissemination of findings.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: Under the supervision of the Senior Qualitative Research Associate, the Qualitative Research Analyst will work collaboratively with program staff and analysts to coordinate qualitative research activities, including conducting literature reviews, designing and implementing study protocols, collecting and analyzing qualitative data, and supporting dissemination activities. 1. Draft qualitative research materials (e.g. protocols, interview guides, and surveys) and support IRB applications. 2. Conduct research literature reviews and desk research, including organizing citation and reference libraries. 3. Collect, clean, manipulate, organize, and analyze qualitative data using Dedoose, REDCap, Excel, and other platforms. 4. Support the Senior Qualitative Research Associate in developing training resources for qualitative methods/analysis and building partnerships with other analytic teams in the agency. 5. Support the creation and revision of study and data management systems related to qualitative research, including qualitative codebooks and analytic plans. 6. Support research administrative tasks including scheduling data collection activities, managing study materials, and gift card tracking and dissemination. 7. Assist with the reporting of qualitative research data, including, but not limited to, internal reporting (e.g., study reports, presentations), external reporting (e.g. conferences), and ad-hoc data requests 8. jobs.description: The Division of Disease Control’s mission is to safeguard the health of New Yorkers through identification, surveillance, treatment, control, and prevention of infectious diseases, which is achieved through varied and interrelated endeavors of its seven Bureaus. The Bureau of Hepatitis, HIV, and Sexually Transmitted Infections’ (BHHS) mission is to improve the lives of New Yorkers by ending transmission, illness, stigma, and inequities related to viral hepatitis, HIV, and sexually transmitted infections. BHHS accomplishes its mission through testing initiatives; prevention, care, and treatment programming; epidemiology and surveillance; training and technical assistance; community engagement; social marketing; policy advocacy; and racial equity and social justice initiatives. BHHS's HIV Care and Treatment Program (CTP) is the Recipient of the Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program (RWHAP) Part A grant, the Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS (HOPWA) grant, and the RWHAP Ending the HIV Epidemic (EHE) cooperative agreement. CTP consists of six units: 1) Quality Management & Program Implementation, 2) Program Planning & Compliance, 3) EHE Initiative Services, 4) Housing Services, 5) Special Projects & Initiatives, and 6) Research and Evaluation.   Reporting to the Manager of Behavioral Health Services, the Quality Management Specialist (Civil Service Title: City Research Scientist I) in the Quality Management & Program Implementation Unit will provide ongoing programmatic and quality management support to community-based organizations, hospitals, and other health facilities that are funded to provide behavioral health services, including psychosocial support and counseling, to people with HIV in New York City. The QMS will work with funded programs to build capacity to manage the quality of services and provide technical assistance to facilitate implementation, gather feedback, ensure fidelity to program models, and confront racism as a driver of health disparities.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Drawing on research and other sources, work with the Manager to propose and apply a range of approaches to developing evidence-based strategies for organizations to provide medical case management and support services to people with HIV. • Provide guidance and support to existing and new programs on the start-up and implementation of program service models for specific target populations to ensure fidelity to protocol and procedures. • Provide coaching in quality management and quality improvement to funded organizations for assigned service categories, both remotely and via site visits. • Advise on the development of quality indicators and quality improvement activities for assigned service categories. • In conjunction with the Manager, propose and implement protocols for reviewing and analyzing performance and quality management data to inform program improvement. • Collaborate with the Research and Evaluation Unit in CTP to evaluate the process of implementing services to provide real-time, actionable feedback on programs to describe and disseminate key findings. • Partner with the Subrecipient Agreement holder (Public Health Solutions) to execute subcontracts and renewals and ensure program integrity and quality through joint monitoring processes. • Review data reported by subcontractors to ensure program integrity and to inform quality management coaching and quality improvement projects. • Assist with planning and implementing meetings, conferences, and other quality management activities provided by the QMPI unit. • Form and maintain relationships with funded organizations, specifically for assigned service categories, and other key stakeholders.  PREFERRED SKILLS: • Knowledge of HIV prevention and treatment, medical case management, populations most affected by HIV (including people aging with HIV), structural determinants of health outcomes, and quality management principles and tools. • Professional working experience with populations most affected by HIV, substance use, mental health, and systems of oppression. • Exceptional relationship-building and influencing skills. • Keen attention to detail and ability to handle multiple and diverse assignments and priorities efficiently and effectively, both independently and as part of a team. • Excellent written, oral communication, organizational, project management and interpersonal skills. • Ability to work effectively with a diverse team, service providers within the NYC Health Department and at external agencies, and clients/consumers who participate in community planning and research review processes. • Proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Adobe Acrobat. • Master of Public Health strongly preferred. jobs.description: The New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (NYC DOHMH)'s Bureau of Hepatitis, HIV, and Sexually Transmitted Infections (BHHS) oversees the City's response to viral hepatitis, HIV, and sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Across a range of programs and through extensive collaboration with other parts of NYC DOHMH and external stakeholders, BHHS leads testing initiatives; prevention, care, and treatment programming; epidemiology and surveillance; research and evaluation; training and technical assistance; community engagement; social marketing; policy advocacy; and racial equity and social justice initiative. The HIV Epidemiology Program (HEP) in the HIV Program in BHHS is responsible for monitoring trends in the HIV epidemic in NYC and developing programming to improve outcomes among people living with and at risk for HIV based on the latest information about the distribution and demographics of HIV in NYC.NYC has a large and diverse HIV epidemic, and programming and analyses of data from HEP inform HIV-related public health policy at the local, state, and national levels. The Core Surveillance Special Projects Unit within HEP is responsible for developing and conducting special projects related to HIV Surveillance such as: expanded HIV surveillance (Project EXPAND) and registry connectivity projects. Expanded HIV surveillance includes developing methods to collect additional data among newly diagnosed persons within priority populations and among those whose primary cause of death was HIV to better describe these populations and identify missed opportunities for HIV prevention. Registry connectivity projects entail linking surveillance data to other electronic medical record systems to provide real-time alerts to providers with the overall purpose of engaging those out of care.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: - Lead and manage all qualitative assurance (QA) activities for Project EXPAND, which include: o QA activities for QDS Warehouse data imports and import logs o Write and maintain SAS code for QA checks of imported interview data o Check completion of tracking sheets and create progress reports for data collectors  o Generate routine reports and tables at end of each interview cycle o Conduct satisfaction assessment surveys to interview participants at the end of each interview cycle  o Present results of QA activities at biweekly team meetings - Act as main liaison with the HIV Surveillance Operations and Core Analysis units in maintaining ongoing investigation list of cases found through interviews with discrepant data. - Assist in training data collectors in Project EXPAND activities. - Maintain QDS CAPI survey instrument, including ongoing CAPI survey programming and related documentation. - Assist Senior Research Analyst in cleaning and analyzing data related to Project EXPAND. - Assist other special projects in QDS CAPI survey programming, piloting and data cleaning. - Conduct data analysis and data dissemination with Core and Special Projects surveillance data. - Contribute to routine HIV surveillance activities including: fulfill data requests, contribute to quarterly analytic datasets, contribute to surveillance annual report, slide sets, surveillance tables, and other dissemination products. - Assist with and contributes to the development of the registry connectivity projects including quality monitoring, data reports, data management and cleaning, and data visualization. jobs.title: Response and Engagement Team Supervisor, Bureau of Community Awareness, Action, Response & Engagement
jobs.description: The Bureau of Community Awareness, Action, Response, and Engagement (BCAARE)’s Community Response and Engagement Unit (CREU) is comprised of Behavioral Health Office of Emergency Preparedness and Response (BHOEPR), Response and Engagement Team (RET),and Triage. CREU clinicians and peers deliver prevention and intervention services to promote mental health, support individual and community adjustment from chronic and acute trauma, support community resilience, and promote community connection. CREU teams assess, assign, and answer requests for behavioral health response, engage communities to provide behavioral health public education and connection to services, and prepare public health staff, first responder personnel, and the public for response to and recovery from events impacting New York City and local communities.   Reporting to the Executive Director, the Response and Engagement Team(RET) Supervisor is responsible for leading and coordinating a multidisciplinary team that responds to urgent community needs, including crises related to public health, behavioral health, and housing instability.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: -Supervise and mentor staff. -Monitor data entry by RET staff, ensuring data integrity and compliance with established procedures and reporting expectations. -Participate with BCAARE’s evaluation team to review outcomes throughout program duration. -Evaluate and monitor monthly progress by creating and reviewing program and productivity metrics. -Integrate evidence-based clinical and research knowledge and strategies supporting community mental health into project activities and initiatives. -Participate in the design and management of evaluation plans for RET including the creation of tools and the development of effective data collection systems and processes for monitoring and reporting on internal and contractor program progress and milestone achievement. -Troubleshoot challenges, issues or concerns that might arise and escalate issues to the ED for direction. -Coordinate with BCAARE’s Office of Data Aggregation, Translation, and Analysis (ODATA), Office of Strategy and Operations, and other teams to review data accuracy, and contribute to data collection processes and analysis, and program development and strategic planning based on data findings. -Follow up and maintain working relationships with NYPD, DHS, SSPs, local CBOs, and other key stakeholders to identify opportunities for coordination and identify contact points to connect community members to services. -Contribute to the interpretation of RET program data to support data-informed decision-making for RET goals and program design. -Hold at least weekly individual supervision with assigned supervisees and coordinate routine group supervision and after-action discussions. -Attend and contribute to all CREU team, cross- bureau, and division-wide meetings. jobs.title: Senior Manager of Capacity Building, Office of Deputy Commissioner
jobs.description: The Center for Health Equity & Community Wellness (CHECW) seeks to eliminate racial and other inequities resulting in premature mortality. With an unwavering grounding in history and structural analysis, CHECW works to increase visibility of the harm perpetuated by centuries of racist, socially unjust policy while pushing towards redress for the most impacted NYC communities. CHECW addresses inequity across community and healthcare systems in partnership with community, faith-based, and health care organizations. CHECW's work focuses on social determinants of health, including health care organizations. CHECW's work focuses on social determinants of health, including environmental and commercial determinants, and addresses both upstream and downstream factors to improve health and well-being of New Yorkers. CHECW is comprised of the Bureau of Bronx Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Brooklyn Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Queens Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention, the Bureau of Equitable Health Systems, the Bureau of Finance and Administrative Services. The division's Deputy Commissioner also serves as the Agency's Chief Equity Officer and oversees Race to Justice, the Agency's internal reform effort to help our staff learn what they can do to better address racial health gaps and improve health outcomes for all New Yorkers. The Health Department launched Race to Justice (RTJ) in 2016 as its agency-wide internal transformation initiative. The primary purpose of the initiative is to build the Health Department's capacity to address structural racism and health inequities by promoting anti racism and embedding racial equity and social justice in our policies, processes, and programs, ensuring that our internal and external practices reflect our values without perpetuating injustices. Spearheaded by the RTJMT, the initiative aims to transform the Health Department by building capacity and embedding racial equity and social justice within every aspect of DOHMH to ultimately improve equitable health outcomes for all New Yorkers by: 1) Increasing staff's awareness of how racism and other intersecting systems of oppression operate within institutions, with the knowledge and understanding that NYC institutions, with the knowledge and understanding that NYC institutions, including the Health Department, are not separate and immune from these systemic injustices. 2) Developing staff's skills to address how internal systems of oppression create health equities. 3) Examining how structural racism and other intersecting systems of oppression impact the Health Department's work, decisions, interactions, and priorities. 4) Implementing policies and practices to mitigate the impacts of systems of oppression.   The Office of the Chief Equity Officer seeks to hire a Senior Manager of Capacity Building to join the management team to build internal capacity among staff to advance racial and social justice and the Health Department's equity goals.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Lead the development and facilitation of communities of practice for agency staff, including equity-focused staff and senior level leadership.  • Organize and/or deliver capacity building trainings and workshops, among other learning activities, focused on embedding equity into daily practices and job responsibilities.  • Evaluate capacity building programs for quality assurance through surveys and analysis of findings.  • Stay abreast of current research, evidence-based best practices, and tools/resources for applying equity in public health.  • Manage, update, and serve as the technical point person for a tool library that includes equity focused tools and resources to assist staff in embedding racial justice and equity.  • Serve as central point of contact for agency equity stakeholder community, including implementing a system of accountability for staff working on projects that advance the goals of the Office of the Chief Equity Officer.  • Connect and coordinate with other team members as it relates to capacity building.  • Contribute to the overall design, strategy, and implementation of Race to Justice activities, as a member of the management team.  PREFERRED SKILLS: Three years of full-time experience in program management, community-based programming, public health, government, or a related field. Excellent oral, written, organizational, and interpersonal communication skills. Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities, work collaboratively across disciplines, and build effective relationships with diverse stakeholders. Strong project management and coordination skills, including the ability to work effectively with government agencies, community organizations, consultants, academic partners, and other external stakeholders  Why you should work for us:  - Loan Forgiveness: As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal/state loan forgiveness and repayment assistance programs that lessen your payments or even fully forgive your full balance. jobs.title: Supervisor of Water Microbiology, Bureau of the Public Health Laboratory
jobs.description: The New York City (NYC) Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) is a public health leader serving over 8.4 million New York City residents from diverse ethnic, cultural, and economic backgrounds. The NYC Public Health Laboratory (PHL) is one of the largest local public health laboratories in the United States offering a dynamic and innovative work environment where employees contribute to the health and safety of NYC residents by providing clinical and environmental laboratory testing services. With more than 100 years of leadership in public health, a team of over 200 scientific and support staff are committed to its mission to safeguard the health of all NYC residents by providing quality laboratory testing services that support the priorities of the NYC DOHMH and its community partners to prevent and respond to clinical and environmental public health concerns.   The DOHMH PHL seeks a qualified candidate to serve as a supervisor in the Environmental Sciences Section. This position will play an integral role in laboratory testing and responding to public health threats, including but not limited to COVID-19, vaccine preventable diseases, HIV, Legionella as well as respiratory, foodborne, and waterborne disease outbreaks. This is an excellent opportunity to join our multidisciplinary team, and collaborate with local, state, federal, and academic partners. The supervisor will primarily work within the Water Microbiology Unit at PHL. The units utilize microbiological and molecular microbiological tools to detect and monitor pathogens in drinking and recreational water, and non-potable water systems such as cooling towers. This includes NYC’s beach monitoring and Legionella response programs. ·   DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Supervising, training, assigning work, and evaluating the performance of staff. Able to shift priorities in response to rapidly evolving work environment. • Conducting investigations regarding agents related to public health outbreaks using independent judgement and initiative, and performing data analysis on test results. Assisting in the coordination of agency, local and federal partners in investigations. • Performing research to identify and implement new technologies. • Communicating effectively with lab technologists and internal and external partners. • Evaluating data, preparing reports, maintaining records, and assisting in the coordination of research efforts of the Agency. • Maintaining and participating in a program of quality control and assurance; and advising staff on appropriate methods and techniques. • Implementing and monitoring laboratory quality, and health and safety policies and procedures. • Performing or overseeing the design and maintenance of charts, logs, and other records. • Assist with inventory, budgeting, and procurement to ensure that laboratory is properly stocked with reagents and supplies necessary for testing; and ensure that items are properly tracked using inventory management system. • Writes original manuscripts for publication based on data analyses. jobs.title: Team Lead: TST for SU & EAU, Bureau of Tuberculosis Control
jobs.description: The Team Lead for TST (SU & EAU) directs tuberculosis surveillance, environmental infection control, and outbreak prevention strategies across DOH chest centers, shelters, and high-risk facilities. In this role, you will manage a multidisciplinary team of research scientists, epidemiologists, and public health advisors conducting quantitative research on airborne tuberculosis detection, managing employee tuberculin skin testing (TST) programs, and overseeing patient isolation protocols. You will evaluate airborne mitigation technologies—such as UVGI, negative pressure, and ACH air-flow systems—to recommend compliant products and establish evidence-based safety guidelines. Additionally, you will oversee outbreak investigations, represent the TB Control Program across internal and external committees, and author scientific papers to publish findings and advance environmental infection control practices statewide.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: - Direct activities and staff of the Tuberculin Skin Testing (TST) Surveillance Unit to meet requirements and fulfill scientific objectives. Ensures that staff in the TST Unit conduct periodic and serial testing of targeted high-risk DOH employees. - Direct activities and staff of the Environmental Affairs Unit to meet requirements and fulfill scientific objectives. - Directs respiratory protection fit testing by the TST Unit and the Environmental Affairs Unit for designated staff in BTBC. - Performs employee evaluations - Serve as a resource to the BTBC for environmental issues pertaining to TB infection control devices and measures including UVG lamps, negatives air pressure, ventilation, and respiratory prevention. - Consults on referrals for patients on home isolation - Provides specialty guidance to Bureau and DOH staff associated with TB outbreaks. - Directs TB related infection control surveys, evaluation, and assessments. - Provides recommendations on infection control and the implementation of environmental controls understanding the standards and guidelines set by the Joint Commission of Accreditation of Health Organizations (JCAHO), CDC, OSHA, PESH, and NIOSH. - Writes technical reports, recommendations, and protocols related to TB transmission. - Plans and implements protocols to develop effective coordination of efforts of the Program and outside projects. - Consults and represents the Program with internal and external entities regarding environmental control of tuberculosis and/or related projects, including providing information regarding design, methodology, sampling procedures, skin testing procedures, and technical matters - Conducts research as indicated, writes papers, and publishes on environmental control of TB  Preferred skills: - Excellent written and oral communication skills  - Experience in research design and intervention - jobs.title: VFC Program Reviewer, Bureau of Immunization
jobs.description: The mission of the Bureau of Immunization (BOI) is to prevent the occurrence and transmission of vaccine-preventable diseases (VPDs) through comprehensive immunization programs. BOI promotes immunization across the lifespan from infancy through adulthood, works to eliminate disparities in vaccination coverage through data evaluation and support of equitable vaccination services, and actively responds to VPD outbreaks to mitigate their spread and impact on communities. The Bureau of Immunization (BOI) is seeking a Research Assistant to work in the Citywide Immunization Registry (CIR) program and the New York City (NYC) Vaccines for Children (VFC) program. The CIR is a central record-keeping system established by the NYC Health Department to collect records of vaccine doses administered in NYC. The CIR consolidates the immunization information and shares it with authorized healthcare providers providing clinical care and vaccination services and agencies concerned with public health. Individuals and guardians can access their own or their minor children’s immunization records from the CIR. Data in the CIR is analyzed for use in monitoring vaccination coverage across NYC and to direct and evaluate public health vaccination programs. The NYC VFC Program distributes federally funded vaccines to private practices, hospitals, and clinics to immunize children aged 0 through 18 years who are eligible for or covered by Medicaid, are uninsured, American Indian/Alaska Native, or whose insurance does not cover the cost of a vaccine. The VFC Unit oversees the review and evaluation of VFC provider practices and is implemented through VFC and Immunization Quality Improvement for Providers (IQIP) site visits. These visits involve vaccine storage and handling evaluations, chart reviews, analysis of electronic immunization records, vaccine ordering, and vaccine utilization and reporting through the CIR. The VFC Unit is also responsible for vaccine management and processing of over 2.6 million doses of publicly funded vaccine for nearly 1,200 immunization providers each year. Providers receive vaccines in accordance with their vaccine reporting to the CIR and the VFC Unit addresses any issues that may require follow-up.   The Research Assistant will perform site visits and medical chart abstractions to ensure providers enrolled in the VFC program are complying with program requirements and best practices. The Research Assistant will also assist provider offices with vaccine ordering and VFC Program re-enrollment, and will participate in outreach activities to recruit and retain providers reporting to the CIR.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Administer in-person or virtually, the Vaccines for Children (VFC) program compliance site visit questionnaire to providers enrolled in the VFC program throughout the five boroughs of NYC to review requirements for vaccine storage and handling, vaccine accountability, vaccine documentation, and appropriate administration of vaccines. • Conduct virtual and/or in-person VFC Immunization Quality Improvement for Providers (IQIP) site visits and collect data pertaining to immunization delivery practices and site-specific immunization coverage, discussion of quality improvement strategies, and delivery of Citywide Immunization Registry (CIR) technical assistance. • Research and prepare vaccine accountability, vaccine coverage and CIR administration reports needed for the site visit. • Research and examine electronic medical record systems to verify patient VFC program eligibility. • Prepare and disseminate after-visit reports to VFC and IQIP program participants. • Document all field activity data in various internal and external tools and systems. • Perform quantitative analysis on site visit data and track progress of site visits. • Assist provider offices with vaccine orders and VFC Program re-enrollment and assist with providing education and information about the VFC program and its requirements. • Use statistical methods to run vaccine coverage reports using CIR and VFC data. • Participate in additional Bureau of Immunization duties as assigned according to civil service title. • Participate in the NYC Health Department’s emergency preparedness and response activities as assigned. jobs.title: Wellness Advocate Supervisor, Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use
jobs.description: The Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use Prevention, Care, and Treatment (BADUPCT) works to close gaps and reduce overall morbidity and mortality related to alcohol and substance use among New Yorkers. BADUPCT develops, implements, and evaluates interventions and prevention strategies through contracting of treatment, recovery and support services; policy analysis and development; epidemiology and surveillance; dissemination of treatment and management guidelines; harm reduction initiatives; public and provider outreach and education; and community involvement and interagency collaboration. The Bureau amplifies the voices of those most impacted and focuses on inequitable structural, social, service, and communication factors that drive disparities.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: Provide research and data support for the expansion of Relay at new hospitals in collaboration with hospital leadership. Conduct research to develop protocols, communications materials, and presentations. Provide regular supervision to full-time and part-time Wellness Advocates in their role supporting patients following a non-fatal overdose and conducting research. Review reports from the program’s database and dashboard on a regular basis to support data-driven supervision. Utilize the program's database to monitor Wellness Advocates' cases to ensure quality assurance standards are being met for research, data collection and data entry, decision making, and overall documentation. Collaborate with colleagues to support the program’s reporting requirements and record observations, including by performing internal auditing activities and assessing participant records. Participate in monthly calls with ED leadership to discuss program implementation and data trends within each collaborating ED. Using program data, lead discussions around the ED staff training needs. Review resumes, screen and interview candidates, hire, orient and on-board new Wellness Advocates. Help to conduct new hire and ongoing trainings for Wellness Advocates responding to non-fatal overdoses. Work collaboratively with other Relay and BADUPCT staff to support the goals and mission of the program and agency. Other duties as assigned.  PREFERRED SKILLS: - Experience practicing public health and working across systems to further a public health approach to alcohol and other drug use. - Experience in working with programs serving people who use drugs, including those using harm reduction approaches. - Experience in managing a budget and/or contracts. - Experience in program monitoring and evaluation. - Experience with quantitative data, including the ability to read, interpret and synthesize epidemiologic and other scientific literature. - Ability to work independently and as part of a team. - Possess exceptional interpersonal, research, written and verbal communication skills. - Detail-oriented with outstanding organizational skills. - Ability to multi-task in a fast-paced, high-volume environment. - Proficiency in Excel, Access, Word, PowerPoint and statistical software such as SPSS or SAS. jobs.description: The New York County District Attorney’s Office is seeking a Senior Investigative Analyst for the Intimate Partner and Sexual Violence Bureau’s (IPSV) IPV Misdemeanor Pre-Arrest Coordination Team (IMPACT) within the Special Victims Division.   IMPACT is a newly established initiative focused on conducting proactive, pre-arrest investigations in IPV misdemeanor cases, strengthening coordination with law enforcement and community partners, and ensuring survivors receive timely access to critical services and resources. The Senior Investigative Analyst will work closely with the Director of IMPACT to identify appropriate cases for pre-arrest investigation, support the development of those investigations, coordinate with internal and external partners, assist in creating and implementing protocols for this new initiative, and maintain and analyze program data. The Analyst will also regularly represent IMPACT and the Office in meetings with the New York City Police Department (NYPD), community-based organizations, and other bureaus and units within the District Attorney’s Office. The position also includes assisting with U visa law enforcement certifications, providing exposure to the intersection of criminal, civil, and immigration law. This position offers a unique opportunity to help shape and implement a new initiative, gain experience with both criminal and civil matters, develop an understanding of immigration law through U visa certification work, and collaborate closely with prosecutors, law enforcement, survivor advocates, community organizations, and other partners.   Responsibilities include but are not limited to:  •	Collaborating closely with the Director of IMPACT to review criminal complaints, domestic incident reports, police reports, and other materials submitted by the New York City Police Department and identify cases appropriate for IMPACT intervention and pre-arrest investigation. •	Assisting with pre-arrest investigations by obtaining and reviewing evidence, generating subpoenas and other records requests, analyzing documents and digital materials, and conducting searches of relevant databases. •	Coordinating with the Survivor Services Bureau by providing advocates with relevant survivors and case information to facilitate survivor outreach and the scheduling of interviews. •	Attending survivor and witness interviews to take detailed notes, assist with case documentation, identify necessary investigative follow-up, and support the development of the investigation. •	Serving as a regular liaison with NYPD personnel, community-based organizations, survivor-service providers, and other external partners regarding IMPACT cases, operations, and initiatives. •	Collaborating with bureaus, units, investigators, analysts, advocates, and other personnel throughout the District Attorney’s Office to facilitate investigations, obtain information, coordinate services, and advance IMPACT initiatives. •	Representing IMPACT and, when appropriate, the District Attorney’s Office at internal and external meetings, working groups, trainings, and community-partner meetings. •	Assisting the Director in developing, documenting, implementing, and refining policies, protocols, workflows, and best practices for IMPACT as the initiative develops and expands. •	Partnering with advocates from the Survivor Services Bureau and outside agencies to coordinate appropriate services, resources, and support for survivors. •	Assisting the Director with the preparation of U visa law enforcement certifications by reviewing case records and related materials to determine whether a matter involves qualifying criminal activity, preparing certification forms and supporting documentation, communicating with immigration attorneys and other relevant parties, and tracking requests through completion. •	Tracking, organizing, and maintaining comprehensive data regarding referrals, investigations, case outcomes, survivor engagement, services, and other IMPACT activities. •	Conducting data collection and analysis to identify trends, measure program activity and outcomes, and support evaluation and continued development of IMPACT. •	Preparing statistical reports, summaries, charts, Excel spreadsheets, PowerPoint presentations, and other materials for internal and external reporting, presentations, program evaluation, and strategic planning. •	Compiling and organizing discovery and other case materials to ensure accurate and timely preparation for legal proceedings. •	Drafting correspondence, memoranda, legal documents, protocols, reports, and other written materials with accuracy and attention to detail. •	Assisting with the development and delivery of training,
