jobs.title: Data Engineer
jobs.description: Description Education Analytics is a non-profit organization that strives to deliver sophisticated, research-informed analytics to educators and school administrators to support their work in improving student outcomes. Data Engineers at EA enable this mission by ensuring that the data educators receive is accurate, up to date, secure, and easily accessible. We are seeking a full-time Data Engineer or Analytics Engineer to join our Engineering team focused on Data & Partners. Candidates for this role may be hired at a Data Engineer II or Senior Data Engineer level depending on skills and experience. The person in this role will design, build, and maintain automated data pipelines and analytic systems for our partner education agencies. This will involve working directly on partner education agency projects to build data systems using EA’s tools, and use the experience of building real systems to advise and contribute to core product development. An ideal candidate has strong SQL skills, experience with data warehousing concepts, and familiarity with complex data integration work. Data engineers are responsible for extract/load processes, data warehouse design, data transformations, and data modeling. While we want our team members to have familiarity with all aspects of ELT, we welcome specialists who may be more experienced on either the data engineering or analytics engineering side. Our typical stack uses an ELT approach via Apache Airflow and dbt to create data warehouses in Snowflake and Databricks. Our team is working to change the education sector by building frameworks to enable collaboration across school systems. To do this, we use open data standards and open-source tools so that solutions we create can be used and re-used in different education agencies across the country. We build and maintain the Enable Data Union project and open-source projects like Earthmover . Our team’s work includes building tools and creating and managing data systems using those tools. This sampling of posts from the Education Analytics blog provides some insight into the role: What we’ve learned building AI on top of Education Data A day in the life of a Data Engineer with Ryan Aguilar A day in the life of a Data Engineer with Angelica Lastra Building Shared Data Infrastructure for Public Education Qualifications 2+ years experience designing data pipelines, systems, and warehouses Knowledge of best design practices in cloud-based data warehouses Knowledge of software engineering practices, particularly in team-based development using Git Fluency in SQL and experience working with real world data Experience with Python Experience with Linux Experience with database administration, security, and management Skills and experience that make you a particularly good fit: Experience with cloud-based columnar data warehouses and other cloud data technologies (Snowflake, RedShift, Databricks, Fabric, BigQuery) Experience working in environments with strict data security requirements Experience with dbt Experience with Apache Airflow Familiarity with AWS tooling and best practices Experience with education data, and the Ed-Fi data standard in particular Experience and interest in using AI code tools as part of development and automation workflows Hiring Process Hiring team reviews applications Selected candidates are invited to submit an asynchronous video interview Selected candidates move on to a second round, which may involve a live remote technical skills assessment Selected candidates are invited for a full day final interview (in person in our downtown Madison office). There will be another approximately 2-3 hours of interviews to meet team members and key members of other teams and to help candidates learn more about Education Analytics & the role. How you will successfully onboard in this role First 30 days: Work through organizational and team onboarding. Get situated into team meetings and one on ones with your manager. Complete a training exercise that familiarizes our new hires with our development setup and tooling. First 60 days: Begin to get involved in your first projects, familiarizing yourself with the project history, context, and goals by joining project meetings and connecting with teammates. Continue familiarizing yourself with our team’s workflow processes and tools. First 90 days: Now fully integrated into your first projects, making regular code and documentation contributions. You may start sharing your development at team meetings. We will start planning for you to take a lead role on sub-tasks within a project. Additional details The weekly expectation is 45 hours per week, and nights and weekends are sometimes required. Our office is in Madison, WI and applicants who live in the area, or are interested in moving here, can work in the office alongside other members of the team. Currently, our engineers include a mix of people who are working from office, hybrid, and fully remote. We are open to remote or on-site candidates for this position. Benefits 9 annual paid holidays, 26.5 days of paid vacation per year, and paid sick time 12% employer 401k contribution + 3% match Generous health benefits Parental leave benefit of up to 26 weeks of paid leave Free Madison Metro transit pass or subsidized office parking (for in person employees) Casual office environment Location right in the heart of downtown Madison, WI Statement on AI Use in Applications We want to hear directly from you! At Education Analytics, we value candidates’ individual experiences, perspectives, and communication styles. To help us fairly assess your qualifications, we ask that candidates prepare their application materials and responses using their own words and experiences. AI tools may be used for proofreading, formatting, and general preparation. However, candidates should not rely on AI to generate substantive answers to application questions, fabricate or embellish qualifications, or complete assessments intended to evaluate their independent skills. Any additional restrictions on AI use during interviews or assessments will be communicated in advance. We appreciate the time and thought you put into applying and look forward to learning more about you. Education Analytics is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

jobs.description: ONLY PERMANENT EMPLOYEES IN THE COMPUTER ASSOCIATE (OPERTAIONS) TITLE AND OTHER EMPLOYEES IN COMPARABLE CIVIL SERVICE TITLES ARE ELIGIBLE TO APPLY.  FISA is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Manager to oversee the FISA-OPA Night Shift D operations team within the Shared Systems division.  The individual must be self-motivated, have a positive attitude, and be willing and able to work with job operations, application, infrastructure, and facilities teams on day-to-day operations and longer-term strategic projects.  The Data Center Operations Shift Manager will take responsibility for their shift in the area of personnel management; printer operations and supplies management; mailing/inserter equipment management; high availability of data center services; vendor management (for print equipment); offsite tape storage operations; mainframe system operator functions; management of the data center equipment and print workspaces; quality control for check print/handling functions;  The Data Center Operations Shift Manager is an essential function of FISA-OPA and requires physical presence at the FISA-OPA location.  The candidate is expected to work through transportation issues and develop alternate transportation plans when necessary.  The individual will develop staffing plans to ensure coverage during normal and peak operational periods.  In addition, the individual will fill in the operator’s role when necessary, in order to ensure continuity of operations.  This is a hands-on position.  The 12 hour/day work schedule will be Mon-Wed or Thu-Sat (alternate week) (with a start time of no later than 19:30 until 8 am) to allow for review of turnover from the night shift.  The individual may be required to provide onsite coverage on Sunday when primary or secondary staff are not available.  Infrequently, the individual may receive escalation calls on Sunday from onsite operators when scheduled for Sunday offsite coverage.  Roles and responsibilities of the Data Center Operations Shift Manager are as follows:  Personnel Management  • Perform resume screening and interviews for new data center operators; development/growth of operator staff; hands-on training or development program for staff to learn mainframe operator tasks and printer/inserter/counter tasks; administration and review of staff performance evaluations • Setup shift to ensure that coverage is in place for:  3 day 12.5hr work shifts with turnover time for hand-off from one shift to the next; rotating Sunday coverage; and holiday coverage • Work with Data Center Manager to re-balance staff between shifts as necessary to ensure minimum required coverage; review overtime usage; planning peak period coverage for periodic check printing, quarterly statement printing, annual tax form printing; • Create (or update) standard operating procedures for documentation data center processes • Prioritize Data Center shift work according to business needs  High Availability of Data Center Services  • The FISA-OPA Data Center is staffed 24x7.  Participate in the electrical, fire prevention/suppression, water detection systems upgrade plans.  Document procedures for data response to data center environmental alerts; • Perform periodic data center walkabout for environmental review & routine inspection of data center IT equipment  Access Management & Coordination with other NYC Agencies using FISA-OPA Data Center  • Serve as point of contact for visitors to the data center • Manage processes to ensure that only authorized staff enter the data center for their shift  Offsite Tape Storage Operations  • Coordinate delivery and / or courier tapes to disaster recovery site tests for their shift • Manage data center operator processes to pull tapes for GRM; interface with application infrastructure teams on the development of tape pull list reports;    Vendor Management  • Serve as a point of contact for auto-mailer (inserter), printer, pre/post print equipment, GRM vendors for their shift • Work with (above) vendors to develop quotes for standard work (moves, minor hardware, etc.); ensure that local technicians are available for service calls and are qualified (capable) to perform work; instruct vendors to store replacement parts onsite in secure lockers (based on useful life and break history)  Mainframe System Operator Functions  • Ensure that processes are followed to actively monitor mainframe online and batch operations; monitor and respond to WTO commands; monitor certain JES queues; vary failed drives offline; start / stop started tasks (per schedule and on request); reprioritize job class assignments for priority workloads;  • Coordinate and execute mainframe LPAR IPLs  Printer Operations and Supplies Management  • Ensure that supplies (envelopes, inserts, check stock, pre-printed forms, roll paper, box paper, etc) are available in the data center stock room in advance of scheduled print jobs; liaison with facilities to ensure that supplies are moved from warehouse to print room floor • Work with Data Center Operations Manager on the ongoing design and implementation of contingency sites for print and inserter operations; coordinate tests of contingency sites • Work with the application team staff during the development of new print forms; ensure that new / updated print forms are run through representative tests and meet FISA-OPA data center print standards (e.g., printed form dimensions, quality, restart capabilities, etc) • Execute projects to upgrade and / or reconfigure printer, cutter & un-winder equipment; coordinate periodic servicing, calibration and maintenance of the printer, cutter & un-winders; ensure that equipment is configured to provide redundancy for all critical print jobs • Under the direction of the Data Center Director:  develop and monitor processes to log check print operations per audit requirements; perform root cause analysis on print equipment failures/errors (e.g., jams, bad cuts, etc.); create and update procedures for use of high-speed printers to accept jobs from Info print and mainframe print queues  Mailing/Inserter Equipment Management  • Ensure that new / updated mail items are run through representative tests and meet FISA-OPA mailing standards (e.g., dimensions and use of AIMS for quality control, alignment with envelope windows, etc); test AIMS software upgrades • Execute tasks for projects to upgrade and / or reconfigure inserter equipment; coordinate periodic servicing, calibration and maintenance of the inserters; ensure that equipment is configured to provide redundancy for all critical print jobs   Management of Data Center Equipment and Print Workspaces  • For work performed on the shift: escalate failure of infrastructure teams to abide by data center workspace policies; enforce procedures that ensure the print room and a clean / clutter free workspace; ensure that items to are discarded as appropriate for shredding; test print jobs are clearly labeled and / or discarded  Quality Control for Check Print/Handling Functions  • The individual will be expected to author and update procedures for quality control of check stock prior to printing; initial checks released to printer for alignment and first check imaged; end of the check run; storage of checks for handling in the morning; voided checks • The individual will be expected to author and update procedures for: use AIMS for reconciliation of expected print forms to inserted print forms; handling of print forms damaged during on auto-mailer; intake and counting of externally printed checks  Distribution and Courier Management  • Coordinate distribution operations with the FISA-OPA Mailroom; OPA Check Distribution Units; FISA-OPA Quality Assurance teams; FISA-OPA Facilities (for transportation of large print jobs); • Provide couriers instructions for delivery assignments to external sites  Preferred Skills/Experience  • Knowledge of IBM Z -15 series mainframe. • Knowledge of TSO. • Familiarity with Tape Auto Library (IBM Preferred). • Familiarity with large laser and Micr Ricoh/OCE printers and Tecnau equipment. • Experience with UNIX Systems a plus. • 10+ years managing large scale Data Center Operations • Knowledge of Neopost check inserter a plus. • Excellent communication (oral and written), interpersonal, and organizational skills. • Ability to work with limited supervision, and to manage multiple deadlines in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. • Excellent troubleshooting, analytical and problem-solving skills. • We are looking for a self-motivated individual who will work well with other groups in an enterprise wide, large-scale matrix environment. Harvard Medical School Information Systems seeks a Business Systems Analyst professional skilled in leading requirements elicitation, journey mapping, business process redesign, and user-centered design. Your Team:  The Office of Housing Access and Stability (“HAS”) consists of the divisions of Housing Opportunity, Tenant and Owner Resources, Housing Stability, Budget and Program Operations, and Program Policy and Innovation. The mission of the office is to ensure fair, efficient, and transparent access to affordable housing. The Office provides subsidies, placement services, and tools that connect New Yorkers to affordable housing and ensures vulnerable households in subsidized housing have the support they need to be safely housed. Housing Access is committed to expanding housing choices, affirmatively furthering fair housing, and stabilizing the financial health of buildings.     The Division of Budget and Program Operations (BPO) within the Office of Housing Access and Stability provides support services to the Division of Housing Opportunity, Division of Tenant and Owner Resources, the Division of Housing Stability, and the Division of Policy and Program Innovation. BPO assists with monitoring and supporting program budgeting and planning, including both staffing and procurement support. The Division also manages the Housing Quality Enforcement and related inspection functions for the Office. In addition, the BPO team coordinates technology initiatives and analytics across the Office in coordination with key technology stakeholders across the agency, providing support on key systems to internal and external stakeholders.   Your Impact:  The City Housing Assistance Program (CHAP) is a city funded rental assistance program administered by the New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD). The program provides rental assistance to low-income households with incomes at or below 50% of Area Median Income (AMI) who are at risk of homelessness, including eligible rent-stabilized households facing eviction for nonpayment of rent and certain households residing in shelter who do not qualify for existing rental assistance programs. CHAP[DN1.1] helps eligible households maintain stable, permanent housing by subsidizing their rent, with the household generally contributing 30% of its adjusted monthly income toward rent. The program provides targeted assistance to New Yorkers facing housing instability while helping preserve rent-stabilized housing and prevent homelessness.    The selected candidate will serve as a Budget Analyst for the division. The Budget Analyst will be responsible for monitoring and working to keep CHAP spending and reporting accurate and complete. This includes running reconciliation reports and communicating with key stakeholders to resolve issues. Additionally, the Analyst will work with internal stakeholders form other Divisions to ensure that funding and expenses issues are resolved in a timely manner. Lastly, the Analyst will work on developing reports and other special projects to proactively address areas of risk within the portfolio. High school graduation or equivalent and six years of experience in community work or community centered activities in an area related to the duties as described above; or  3. We also do not work with external recruiting agencies, so outreach from headhunters presenting opportunities on behalf of Khan Academy is illegitimate. ABOUT KHAN ACADEMY Khan Academy is a nonprofit with the mission to deliver a free, world-class education to anyone, anywhere. Our proven learning platform offers free, high-quality supplemental learning content and practice that cover Pre-K - 12th grade and early college core academic subjects, focusing on math and science. We have over 181 million registered learners globally and are committed to improving learning outcomes for students worldwide, focusing on learners in historically under-resourced communities. ABOUT KHAN ACADEMY KIDS Khan Academy Kids is a free and fun learning program for children ages 2 to 8. Kodi Bear and a cast of animated characters lead children on a personalized education journey filled with fun, standards-aligned activities in early literacy, math, executive functioning and social emotional skills. Built by a small but mighty team, Khan Academy Kids is used by millions of children in homes and classrooms around the world. OUR COMMUNITY Our students, teachers, and parents come from all walks of life, and so do we. Our team includes people from academia, traditional/non-traditional education, big tech companies, and tiny startups. We hire great people from diverse backgrounds and experiences because it makes our company stronger. We value diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging as necessary to achieve our mission and impact the communities we serve. We know that transforming education starts in-house with learning about ourselves and our colleagues. We strive to be world-class in investing in our people and commit to developing you as a professional. THE ROLE Khan Academy Kids is looking for a Senior Efficacy Research and Psychometrics Analyst (24 months fixed-term) to strengthen the evidence base behind our assessments and learning content for children in PreK through 2nd grade. This role spans two complementary areas. First, you will lead the technical side of our psychometrics and efficacy research: serving as the primary point of contact for our external research partners, managing recurring data extracts, analyzing and interpreting psychometric findings, and helping translate research into product improvements. Second, you will own analytics and reporting for Khan Academy Kids: building and maintaining our KPI dashboard and preparing the recurring reporting that our leadership, philanthropy, and school partnerships teams rely on to make decisions and tell our impact story. You will work on a small, interdisciplinary team alongside product managers, engineers, designers, and academic experts and collaborate closely with leading external research organizations. We are looking for someone with strong quantitative training — ideally in psychometrics, educational measurement, or a related field — who is energized by using rigorous evidence to improve learning experiences for young children. Responsibilities: (1) Psychometrics & Efficacy Research Lead our psychometric research partnership : Serve as the primary technical point of contact for our external psychometric research partnership, supporting study design, data sharing, psychometric analyses, and interpretation of findings Extract, clean, and securely share assessment data with research partners on a recurring schedule Analyze and interpret psychometric findings, including item difficulty, score distributions, growth analyses, concurrent validity, and IRT-based scoring Partner with our product and engineering teams to translate findings into product improvements, such as updates to scoring models and assessment discontinuation rules Collaborate with research partners to develop and publish technical documentation, beginning with the technical manual for our PreK assessment Recruit and manage research partner sites: Recruit and onboard school and district sites for psychometric and efficacy studies; execute MOUs; align on consent procedures and participant incentives; and coordinate site visits for direct child assessment data collection Partner with our legal team to draft and negotiate data-sharing agreements with districts and research organizations, including requirements for pseudonymized and identified data Support efficacy research. Coordinate Khan Academy Kids' participation in ongoing efficacy studies and contribute to the design of future studies, aligning internal and external stakeholders on the research approach (2) Analytics Reporting and Data Infrastructure Own Khan Kids’s KPI dashboard: Partner with our engineering team to build and maintain the Khan Academy Kids analytics dashboard, including integrations with App Store Connect and Google Play Console. Maintain the dashboard so it can be used by other teams including marketing, school partnerships, and philanthropy. Lead recurring reporting: Prepare recurring app performance reporting, including monthly and quarterly business reviews and periodic target setting. Field ad hoc data requests across teams — for example, writing new SQL queries to support targeted district outreach or grant reporting. WHAT YOU BRING An advanced degree (PhD or Master's) in psychometrics, educational measurement, quantitative methods or a related field — or equivalent applied experience Strong grounding in psychometric methods, including item analysis, reliability and validity evidence, growth modeling, and Item Response Theory (IRT) Proficiency with SQL and a statistical programming language (e.g., R or Python) for extracting, cleaning, analyzing, and visualizing data Experience with (or eagerness to learn) business intelligence tools such as Looker, and comfort building dashboards and data pipelines Familiarity with responsible data-sharing practices in education research, including student data privacy considerations (e.g., FERPA, COPPA) and work with pseudonymized and deidentified data Excellent communication skills: able to translate complex psychometric findings into clear implications for product teams, funders, and school partners Strong project-management and organizational skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple external partners, recurring deliverables, and data-sharing schedules with close attention to detail Proven cross-cultural competency skills, demonstrating self-awareness, awareness of others, and the ability to adopt inclusive perspectives, attitudes, and behaviors to drive inclusion and belonging throughout the organization Motivated by Khan Academy’s mission “to provide a free, world-class education for anyone, anywhere” Nice to have: Experience with (or strong interest in) early childhood education and assessment of young learners is a plus PERKS AND BENEFITS We may be a non-profit, but we reward our talented team extremely well! This belief is why we have built out a robust Total Rewards package that includes competitive base salaries, and extensive benefits and perks to support physical, mental, and financial well-being. jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer
jobs.description:
About Kiddom

Kiddom is transforming K–12 education by bringing high-quality curriculum, instructional tools, and student analytics together in one coherent system. We are building Learning Intelligence Technology (LIT), a new category that gives educators the infrastructure to plan, teach, assess, and respond to student needs. With Kiddom, educators spend less time managing administrative burden and more time delivering meaningful student instruction. Kiddom helps schools and districts deliver more equitable, effective, and adaptive learning experiences.

We're looking for a Senior Data Engineer to join Kiddom's Content & AI Systems team, building the data layer that powers next-generation AI-assisted curriculum authoring and content delivery. You'll own the pipelines, schemas, and validation frameworks that turn messy, domain-specific curriculum content into structured, AI-ready data products, working closely with Instructional Designers, AI engineers, and the Content Agents team. This role suits an engineer who's comfortable in a non-traditional data engineering space and energized by defining data requirements and infrastructure from the ground up.


You will:

 - Design and own the schema and data models representing Kiddom’s curriculum content (lessons, activities, standards alignments) for downstream use 

 - Build ingestion pipelines that process content from varied, inconsistent source formats — XML, JSON, PDF-derived, and API-delivered

 - Develop Python-based parsers, transformers, and validation scripts that enforce schema conformance and content quality at scale 

 - Collaborate directly with Instructional Designers and product teams to translate content authoring workflows into data engineering requirements

 - Build and maintain embedding and vector database pipelines that feed Kiddom’s AI-powered content features as they scale

 - Work in Git-based workflows — treating data artifacts with the same rigor as software: versioned, reviewed, and documented

What we're looking for:

 - 4+ years of data engineering experience with strong Python skills — you’ve written parsers, validators, and transformation scripts for real-world messy data

 - Schema design instincts — you think carefully about how data should be structured for downstream use, not just how to move it 

 - Data quality mindset — you build validation and completeness checks in from the start, not as an afterthought 

 - Cross-functional collaborator — comfortable working with non-engineers to define requirements and translate domain knowledge into data structures

 - Provisioning and monitoring of infrastructure for data systems, familiarity with IaC tools such as Terraform and Terragrunt

 - The data system operates, ECS, EKS clusters, provision lambdas and S3 buckets

 - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in CS or equivalent work experience

Nice to Have: 

 - Background in education, curriculum design, or ed-tech — understanding how instructional content is authored and structured is a genuine differentiator

 - Experience with vector databases (Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector) or embedding pipeline tooling 

 - Familiarity with agentic AI patterns or Model Context Protocol (MCP)

 

What we offer

 - Full time permanent employees are eligible for the following benefits from their first day of employment:

 - Competitive salary

 - Meaningful equity

 - Health insurance benefits: medical (various PPO/HMO/HSA plans), dental, vision, disability and life insurance

 - 401k plan

 - One Medical membership (in participating locations)

 - Flexible vacation time policy (subject to internal approval). Average use 4 weeks off per year.

 - 10 paid sick days per year (pro rated depending on start date)

 - Paid holidays

 - Paid bereavement leave

 - Paid family leave after birth/adoption. Minimum of 16 paid weeks for birthing parents, 10 weeks for caretaker parents. Meant to supplement benefits offered by State.

 - Commuter and FSA plans


Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

Kiddom is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, religion, color, gender, sexual orientation, transgender status, national origin, citizenship status, uniform service member status, pregnancy, age, genetic information, disability, or any other protected status in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws.

jobs.description: Overview Build the Future At McGraw Hill, we are dedicated to delivering digital learning experiences that transform education for learners and educators. Our focus is on creating seamless, impactful products that truly benefit our users while supporting growth and collaboration across teams. We foster a culture that values innovation, teamwork, and a balance between career growth and personal well-being. We’re seeking a Strategic Sourcing Analyst to join our Global Procurement team. How can you make an impact? The Strategic Sourcing Analyst is part of the Strategic Sourcing organization within Global Procurement. You will join a collaborative, high-performing team focused on delivering enterprise value through disciplined sourcing, market insight, and strong business partnership. In this role, you will support strategic sourcing initiatives across indirect procurement categories by transforming data into actionable insights, conducting market and supplier research, and producing structured materials that enable sourcing decisions. Your work will help ensure sourcing activities are well-documented, compliant with procurement governance, and positioned to drive measurable outcomes. Success in this role is demonstrated through high-quality analysis, dependable execution, and proactive collaboration with stakeholders in Finance, Legal, Procurement Operations, and business teams. Reporting to a Manager of Strategic Sourcing and working remotely from a home office, this is a critical position for supporting the Strategic Sourcing organization. This position may travel 3-4 times per year for in-person meetings. This role is open to applicants authorized to work for any employer in the United States. What you will be doing: Category Strategy & Market Insight Build foundational understanding of assigned categories, supplier landscape, and basic market dynamics; maintain category and supplier profiles. Gather and synthesize market information including benchmarks, trends, cost drivers to support category planning and sourcing events. Commercial & Negotiation Capability Support sourcing events (RFI/RFP/RFQ) by preparing bid comparisons, pricing summaries, and evaluation templates. Supports contract negotiations through analysis, documentation, and comparison of commercial terms, working under the guidance of senior team members and in partnership with Legal. Assist with documenting commercial terms, assumptions, and recommendation rationale for stakeholder review. Stakeholder & Influence Skills Respond to requests from internal stakeholders and team leaders clearly and professionally; communicate status and dependencies. Coordinate inputs across cross-functional partners including Finance, Legal, Risk, Procurement Operations to support sourcing timelines and deliverables. Analytical & Financial Acumen Perform accurate spend analysis and basic pricing comparisons; validate data integrity and resolve discrepancies. Build and maintain dashboards and tracking tools that provide transparency into sourcing pipeline, status, and outcomes. Risk, Governance & Compliance Follow procurement policies and governance standards; ensure required documentation is complete, accurate, and audit-ready. Identify potential commercial or process risks during sourcing activities and escalate appropriately. Leadership & Talent Development Demonstrate accountability, intellectual curiosity, and continuous learning; seek feedback to improve analytical quality and sourcing effectiveness. Contribute to team knowledge sharing through documentation and incorporation of learnings into templates and tools. We’re looking for someone with: Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Supply Chain, Economics, or related field, or equivalent experience. 2+ years of relevant experience in analytics, procurement, sourcing, finance, or a related discipline. Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy. Ability to structure analysis and communicate findings in clear, concise formats. Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools (Excel, PowerPoint, Word); comfort working with data sets and dashboards. Ability to coordinate multiple tasks, meet deadlines, and operate effectively in a team environment. Professional communication skills and an orientation toward customer and stakeholder support. Willingness to learn procurement policies, basic commercial terms, and sourcing governance expectations. Preferred: Exposure to sourcing tools, contract repositories, or procurement workflows. Foundational understanding of commercial and contractual terms, with the ability to support negotiation activities through analysis, documentation, and coordination with Legal and stakeholders. Experience with basic financial modeling or spend analysis techniques. Why work for us? The work you do at McGraw Hill will be work that matters. We are collectively designing content that will build the future of education. Play your part and experience a sense of fulfillment that will inspire you to even greater heights. jobs.description: Overview Build the Future At McGraw Hill, we are dedicated to delivering digital learning experiences that transform education for learners and educators. Our focus is on creating seamless, impactful products that truly benefit our users while supporting growth and collaboration across teams. We foster a culture that values innovation, teamwork, and a balance between career growth and personal well-being. How can you make an impact? The Technology Sourcing Analyst supports sourcing strategies and transactions across software, SaaS, cloud, hardware, AI, network, and technology services. The role performs commercial analysis, coordinates sourcing activities, and independently manages straightforward renewals and low-complexity deals to support supplier decisions, negotiations, and measurable value delivery. Working within established commercial and contracting parameters, the Analyst gathers requirements, analyzes supplier proposals and pricing, negotiates routine transactions, supports contract reviews, and coordinates cross-functional activities with Technology, Security, Privacy, Finance, Legal, and business stakeholders. Success is demonstrated through accurate and timely analysis, disciplined execution, complete documentation, proactive communication, and effective management of assigned deliverables. This is a remote position open to applicants authorized to work for any employer within the United States. What You’ll Do: Category Strategy & Market Insight Gather market, supplier, pricing, license, consumption, and performance information to support category strategies and sourcing plans. Maintain category data, benchmarks, supplier profiles, renewal calendars, and sourcing pipeline information. Commercial & Negotiation Capability Independently manage and negotiate straightforward renewals and low-complexity technology transactions; coordinate defined RFPs, supplier evaluations, and commercial workstreams, and support sourcing leaders on more complex or higher-risk deals. Prepare bid analyses, pricing comparisons, cost and TCO models, savings calculations, and negotiation materials across subscription, licensing, consumption, services, and hardware pricing models. Review and negotiate standard technology agreements, order forms, renewals, amendments, and lower-complexity supplier-provided contracts within established parameters; identify and escalate non-standard pricing, scope, service-level, renewal, audit, termination, data, security, or transition terms. Stakeholder & Influence Skills Coordinate requirements, supplier communications, evaluations, approvals, and action items with Technology and cross-functional stakeholders; communicate negotiation outcomes and escalate exceptions requiring additional review. Analytical & Financial Acumen Perform pricing, benchmarking, savings, cost-avoidance, TCO, utilization, and scenario analyses using established methods and templates. Maintain value tracking, sourcing reporting, contract data, and supporting records; verify data accuracy and follow up on missing information. Risk, Governance & Compliance Maintain complete sourcing and contracting documentation in accordance with procurement governance and audit requirements. Identify commercial, contractual, operational, or supplier risks; resolve routine issues within established guidance and escalate material risks or exceptions. Leadership & Talent Development Use and help improve sourcing templates, playbooks, reports, and standard processes. Build knowledge of technology categories, supplier markets, commercial models, and sourcing practices through assigned work and team collaboration. What You Bring: Bachelor's degree required; relevant procurement, finance, business, technology, or supply chain experience may be considered where appropriate. 2+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, procurement analytics, finance, supply chain, contract administration, or a related field. Experience supporting sourcing events and independently managing straightforward renewals or low-complexity commercial transactions. Strong analytical skills with experience preparing pricing comparisons, savings analyses, cost models, or business summaries. Ability to organize supplier and stakeholder inputs, manage assigned deadlines, negotiate within established parameters, and produce accurate deliverables. Working knowledge of technology commercial models and contracts, including software licensing, SaaS subscriptions, hardware, cloud or consumption pricing, order forms, SOWs, service levels, renewals, and amendments. Ability to identify and resolve routine commercial issues and escalate non-standard terms, risks, or exceptions with supporting facts. Strong written and verbal communication, attention to detail, and proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Preferred Experience: Experience negotiating software or SaaS renewals, low-complexity technology deals, standard order forms, amendments, or supplier-provided agreements. Familiarity with sourcing platforms, contract lifecycle processes, procurement governance, or supplier performance reporting. Progress toward a professional certification such as CPSM or CIPS, or equivalent. Why work for us? The work you do at McGraw Hill will be work that matters. We are collectively building experiences that will help shape the future of education. Play your part and experience a sense of fulfilment that will inspire you to even greater heights. jobs.title: :    Executive Office Coordinator & Policy Analyst, NYC Housing Preservation Trust
jobs.description: On June 16, 2022, Governor Kathy Hochul signed the NYC Public Housing Preservation Trust Act, which authorized creation of the NYC Public Housing Preservation Trust (the Trust). The Trust is a public benefit corporation that will oversee the renovation and rehabilitation of the city’s public housing developments, owned by the New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA). NYCHA remains permanent owner of the land/buildings and enters into a long-term ground lease with the Trust to secure a Section 8 rental subsidy contract with significantly higher value than NYCHA’s current federal subsidy. Using the rental subsidy contract, the Trust will raise financing to fund comprehensive building renovations. The Trust Act provides the Trust with the ability to convert up to 25,000 units, subject to a vote by the residents of a potential redevelopment site. No NYCHA site can convert to the Trust without a positive vote of the site’s residents. To date, residents at four developments have opted into the Trust, resulting in over 1,700 units that will be financed and renovated over the next five years, providing benefits to over 3,200 residents.   Our values are core to our work. The Trust has adopted the following values:  1)	Resident Empowerment: Center your efforts on the voices, needs, and leadership of residents in all aspects of the Trust’s operations. Actively engage and empower residents to foster stable, safe, and thriving communities.  2)	Action-Oriented Excellence: Commit to urgent and effective action while maintaining a dedication to high-quality outcomes. Drive impactful results with a focus on excellence.  3)	Future-Forward Resilience: Prepare our communities and buildings for the challenges of climate change and the future. Focus on creating resilient and sustainable environments to ensure long-term safety and adaptability.  4)	Informed Innovation: Integrate innovative ideas and best practices into our approach to public housing. Continuously improve and lead in the field by leveraging a network of global peers with similar missions and values.  5)	Collaborative Strength: Embrace the power of partnerships between the Trust, NYCHA, and various stakeholders. Involve multiple agencies and partners in finance, design, engineering, social services, training, and community rebuilding to transform public housing communities.   Position Summary  The Executive Office Coordinator & Policy Analyst serves within the Office of the President and reports directly to the Chief of Staff. The position provides policy analysis, executive support, and governance coordination for the President, Chief of Staff, and Board of Trustees.  Working at the intersection of strategy, operations, and public policy, the Coordinator/Policy Analyst researches emerging policy issues, prepares executive briefings and Board materials, supports organizational policy development, and manages cross-functional initiatives that advance the Trust's mission.  The position requires exceptional analytical, writing, project management, and organizational skills. The successful candidate will be equally comfortable conducting policy research, synthesizing complex information into executive-level recommendations, coordinating Board governance activities, and managing high-priority initiatives across multiple departments.  As part of a newly established public benefit corporation, the Coordinator/Policy Analyst will play an important role in helping shape organizational policies, governance practices, and strategic initiatives supporting one of the nation's largest public housing preservation efforts. jobs.title: Contract & Procurement Analyst
jobs.description: The New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) is the nation’s oldest and largest public housing authority with more than 177,000 apartments, and responsibility for administering a citywide Section 8 leased housing program that serves over 150,000 additional tenants. NYCHA’s mission is to provide quality housing for New Yorkers that is sustainable, inclusive, and safe, while fostering opportunities for economic mobility.  NYCHA’s Asset & Capital Management (A&CM) Division leads the Authority’s capital, sustainability and resiliency programs that comprise a $6 billion capital projects portfolio - one of the largest in NY State - as well as a range of activities related to property modernization and strategic asset management. A&CM aims to preserve and modernize NYCHA buildings and apartments through strategic portfolio planning, comprehensive design standards, innovative financing and project delivery models, strong partnership with NYCHA residents and other stakeholders, and effective program and project management of capital investments. The Division also positions NYCHA’s housing portfolio for the future by piloting and scaling-up sustainable and resilient technologies and practices, improving residents’ quality of life while enhancing building performance. The work culture of the Division is strongly customer service oriented, collaborative and delivery-focused.  Strategic Services comprises five diverse teams who provide key business services and drive operational excellence across A&CM. Core functions of Strategic Services include: leading capital planning and financial administration including cost estimating for capital projects; supporting business departments to apply best-practice project management and project controls frameworks; enabling strategic vendor and contract management services; providing business intelligence services across the division to ensure data-driven management and decision-making; and, supporting business operations through supporting human resources management and logistics administration. Reporting directly to the Deputy Director for Contract Management, the Contract & Procurement Analyst performs complex professional, analytical, and administrative work supporting the full lifecycle of procurement and contract administration activities for A&CM contracts and associated task orders. The Contract & Procurement Analyst works closely with internal departments, Procurement, Law, Finance, oversight agencies, and other stakeholders to facilitate timely contract actions, maintain compliance, analyze and resolve procurement and contract administration issues, and support effective contract portfolio management. In the absence of the Deputy Director, the Contract & Procurement Analyst may represent the Department at meetings and coordinate contract-related activities with internal and external stakeholders. ENDGBV Budget Modification Requests: •	Review current modified budgets and financial information in FMS. •	Prepare budget modification requests in accordance with applicable procedures and requirements. •	Reconcile figures included in budget modification requests against current FMS records to ensure accuracy and consistency. •	Submit completed requests to the supervisor for review and approval. •	Track outstanding modifications and follow up as needed to support timely completion.  2. Role Type: Full-time Compensation : $97,000 Visa sponsorship: Not available Hires remotely in: United States Experience: 2+ years of full-time, professional work experience Recidiviz is thrilled to be hiring a Data Analyst to join our team! We’re a small, fast-moving group that works with complex criminal justice data from our state partners and develops analyses and tools that target the drivers of incarceration. That’s where you come in. We’re looking for someone who has attention to detail to improve our analysis, creativity and inquisitiveness to identify and solve open-ended problems, clarity to think through complex and variable data, flexibility to adjust in a rapidly evolving environment, and above all else, a collaborative, kind nature to add to our culture. About us Recidiviz is creating safer, healthier communities by improving outcomes for people in the criminal justice system. We build technology to reduce the number of people in prison and to help criminal justice leaders embrace data-driven decision-making. Using software tools and thoughtful product design, we’ve been able to safely and permanently reduce incarceration and improve outcomes. We work side-by-side with leaders of the criminal justice system, people in prison and on supervision, and ecosystem partners to build a better path forward. In addition to the revenue we earn from state partners, some of the most respected philanthropists and foundations support our work. People who succeed at Recidiviz lead with kindness and humility, assume good intent, learn from failure, and fix problems when they see them. They are excited to work arm in arm with government leadership and staff to improve outcomes. They are great listeners. They build deep relationships with and empathy for the people we work with and the people who our mission serves, even when those two groups feel at odds. About the role This role collaborates across several teams to guide work that targets the drivers of incarceration. Our Data Analysts work with diverse data – criminal justice data both raw and processed from across the country, reports and policy documents from government agencies, and much more – to develop our understanding of the criminal justice system and to motivate change. They perform analyses, contribute to tooling that improve our data and how we work with it, and help drive product launches by ensuring each product in each state has the analytical data required to drive the impact we seek. How do the factors that drive parole board decisions align with the factors most quantitatively predictive of post-release outcomes? How would outcomes change if dynamic factors were weighted more heavily? How will a new supervision contact standard affect the alignment between supervision officer bandwidth and high-need clients? By translating policy concepts into concrete modeling, we help states make smarter and more ambitious changes. Senior Policy Data Analysts are high-autonomy technical contributors. They own an end to end analytic process — breaking project objectives into analytical products, designing the approach, derisking the timeline, producing the findings, and preparing the materials that go in front of decision-makers. The core skill is decision-support: building analysis for a decision rather than for a research finding. This role is as much about making judgment calls as it is about running analytical work. Most of our projects are first of their kind, which requires designing the approach as you go. Projects change mid-flight as our understanding of system dynamics develops and the needs of stakeholders shift. This role works closely with a Partnerships Lead, who coordinates with state partners to determine project objectives. The Senior Policy Data Analyst sets the analysis strategy to meet those objectives. Success is measured by the impact your interventions drive. You ramp up on new data quickly, going deep where it changes the answer and making defensible simplifying assumptions where it doesn’t. Modeling policy scenarios and quantifying tradeoffs . Apply statistical methods like regressions, time series, stock-and-flow modeling or distributional analysis to project how outcomes change under different policy designs, and assess what the data can and can't support. A core judgment is developing simple and elegant approaches that cut to the heart of the decision point. Communicating findings to the people making the decision . You work backward from what information a stakeholder needs to advance decision-making in the room. You'll create the decks and memos that go to DOC leadership, find the frameworks that make a complicated tradeoff digestible, and take responsibility for tailoring your work to the audience to motivate action . You'll collaborate across the organization to obtain state context, understand underlying data infrastructure, and support policy implementation. Finding the next opportunity. You’ll go deeper on the states you work in — spotting where additional analysis could unlock a decision, and running the early exploration to assess whether it’s worth pursuing. jobs.description: The Stanford Department of Neurology has been a center of excellence for more than four decades and supports one of the top research programs in the U.S. with over 200 faculty serving as leaders in the neurological sciences. The Department of Neurology is seeking a highly motivated Research Administrator 3 (RA3) to support our faculty Principal Investigators (PIs) as they seek external research funding. This position is focused on pre-award administration, and this person will play a critical role in advancing the departments’ research enterprise. This person will serve as a resource expert and manage the preparation of complex research proposals, including grants, contracts, program projects, and cooperative agreements involving multiple PIs, multiple subaward sites, and varied cross-school initiatives. The role will also provide an opportunity to mentor staff and lead process improvement projects. The RA3 will have a passion for supporting research, thrive on complexity, possess exceptional attention to detail, be adept in multitasking, and bring a resourceful and collaborative approach to the work. This person will also have excellent communication skills in order to advocate for PIs within Stanford’s diverse academic and medical community. DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS: Certified Research Administrator (CRA) certification. Complex proposal preparation experience in an academic environment. Experience managing multiple projects and timelines in a dynamic research setting. Extreme attention to detail. Working knowledge of sponsored project guidelines and the research regulatory environment. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS*: Frequently sit, grasp lightly, use fine manipulation and perform desk-based computer tasks, lift, carry, push and pull objects weighing up to ten pounds. Occasionally stand, walk, grasp forcefully, use a telephone, write by hand and sort and file paperwork or parts. Rarely lift, carry, push and pull objects weighing 11-20 pounds. * - Consistent with its obligations under the law, the University will provide reasonable accommodation to any employee with a disability who requires accommodation to perform the essential functions of his or her job. WORK STANDARDS: Interpersonal Skills: Demonstrates the ability to work well with Stanford colleagues and clients and with external organizations. Promote Culture of Safety: Demonstrates commitment to personal responsibility and value for safety; communicates safety concerns; uses and promotes safe behaviors based on training and lessons learned. Subject to and expected to comply with all applicable University policies and procedures, including but not limited to the personnel policies and other policies found in the University's Administrative Guide, http://adminguide.stanford.edu . ADDITIONAL DUTIES*: Coordinate preparation and submission of NIH Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPRs) by working with PIs, ORO, post-award teams, and collaborators; collect financial and progress data; develop checklists and timelines; ensure compliance with sponsor and institutional policies. Maintain and update Other Support documentation with PIs and post-award teams; verify completeness and compliance to support timely submission for Just in Time requests, progress reports, and internal reviews. * - Other duties may also be assigned. Core Duties : Prepare complex proposals within parameters of sponsored and non-sponsored research guidelines. Oversee and communicate submission process, both paper and electronic; resolve issues relating to proposal preparation and submittal process. Develop, prepare, revise, and finalize project budgets, and provide budget justification; obtain cost sharing commitment and support. Serve as liaison and active partner between principal investigators, Office of Sponsored Research, research groups, and other departments; respond to sponsor inquiries; advise of new regulations. Collaborate with Office of Sponsored Research to ensure awards are set up properly and cost-sharing requirements are fulfilled; initiate cost transfers. Review and approve expenditures, advise on post award spending and commitment activity, and oversee compliance related to fund and revenue. Develop and communicate reports supporting project status; create forecasting models, scenarios, and decision aides. Manage contract closeout process and audit inquiries; submit final reports and certificates. Interpret complex university and government policies (FAR, Cost Accounting Standards, Office of Management and Budget circulars, sponsored guidelines, etc.) for project and university personnel and help guide other staff in interpreting complex policies. Identify and implement process improvements. Participate in and lead cross campus projects. Train and advise on issues requiring specific technical expertise. Oversee and review work of other staff. May supervise, train and mentor other staff. Serve as a resource on subject area to principal investigator staff. Minimum Education and Experience Bachelor’s degree and five years of job-related experience, or combination of education and relevant experience. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities : Expert knowledge and fluency of governmental regulations (e.g. FAR, Uniform Guidance, CAS). Knowledge and ability to understand, interpret, and communicate university policies and procedures. Excellent oral, written, and communication skills. Excellent analytical skills; demonstrated proficiency in Excel and web-based tools. Strong accounting skills; knowledge of accounting principles. Knowledge of procurement needs, including sole-sourcing, cost analyses, vendor requirements, and small business reporting. Strong knowledge of property management requirements related to Stanford or non-Stanford title of equipment and fabrications. jobs.title: Social Science Research Scholar (1-Year Fixed Term) (Remote Opportunity)
jobs.description: The Division of Primary Care and Population Health seeks to serve our community through caring, learning, and innovation for the whole person through all stages of live. While engaged in practice and teaching, our faculty are dedicated to establishing new knowledge as the basis for future practice and prevention, and to the greatest extent possible applying that knowledge to improve care for all and reduce health disparities. The research scholar will take a leadership role in Pascal Geldsetzer’s research group, which is a “dry lab” focused on quantitative analyses of existing, and often publicly accessible, datasets. The group works on a wide variety of research topics, with current foci being the causal effect of shingles vaccination on cognition ( https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.1101/2023.05.23.23290253v1 ), the health effects of sodium intake, and population health issues more generally. Key data sources for projects are large population-based cohort studies, electronic health record data, mortality data, and other large health-related administrative datasets. The group is also working on randomized intervention studies in low- and middle-income country settings and the re-analysis of clinical trial data. The researcher will be expected to publish in high-impact peer-reviewed journals. We are in particular looking for individuals with in-depth experience in econometric/quasi-experimental approaches for causal effect estimation (e.g., regression discontinuity and difference-in-differences). We are looking for someone to start as soon as possible but there is no specific deadline for the application – we hire on an ongoing basis. The initial appointment will be 1-year fixed term. The fixed term may be renewed for additional years based on business needs. This is a remote eligible position. CORE DUTIES: Carrying out data analyses Supervising data analyses led by graduate students and postdoctoral fellows Writing manuscripts for publication in scientific journals Mentoring and advising junior researchers Assisting with, and leading the writing of, grant applications for research funding Communicating with research funders, data providers, and project administrative staff EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE: Doctoral degree with quantitative training or research experience. Training and experience in quasi-experimental techniques (regression discontinuity, difference-in-differences, interrupted time-series, etc.) A background in health-related research is a plus but not required KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES: Strong coding skills in R, Stata, or other statistical software package. Strong writing and analytical skills. Ability to prioritize workload.

jobs.description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION AND THE OPPORTUNITY The Education Trust (Ed Trust) seeks a Senior Research Analyst in our New York office (ETNY). The Senior Research Analyst will join a staff committed to fulfilling our mission of closing opportunity gaps that disproportionately affect students of color and students from low-income backgrounds. The Senior Analyst serves as a content expert on quantitative and qualitative research, advancing research and policy priorities in alignment with EdTrust-New York’s strategic goals. This role will produce research that highlights trends and inequities for students of color and students from low income backgrounds. The Senior Analyst will develop analyses, research briefs, data tools and visualizations, presentations, and other communications that advance, promote, and elevate strengths and opportunities for increasing educational equity in New York City and across the state. Successful candidates will bring knowledge of and ability to access and analyze publicly available education datasets in New York State and New York City through an education equity lens. Ed Trust is committed to advancing policies and practices to dismantle the racial and economic barriers embedded in the U.S. education system. Through our research and advocacy, Ed Trust improves equity in education from preschool through college, engages diverse communities dedicated to equity and justice, and increases political and public will to build an education system where all students will thrive. Available immediately, this role is based in our New York office and works primarily from a home office in New York or New Jersey. The Senior Analyst reports to the Lead II of Research. ABOUT THE SENIOR ANALYST, RESEARCH ROLE The responsibilities and objectives for the role include, but are not limited to, the following: · Develop and conduct quantitative analyses - using publicly available data - that examine socioeconomic and race-based patterns in opportunity and success, leveraging coding skills and analytics software to conduct descriptives and subgroup analyses. · Develop and conduct qualitative analyses; including original data collection that examine socioeconomic and race-based patterns in opportunity and success, leveraging focus groups, survey instruments, and analyses software. · Manage and implement multiple projects that identify promising policies for advancing educational equity, including producing tools and resources for diverse audiences (e.g., students, policymakers, families, and institutional leaders) · Mine data from publicly available sources to produce replicable datasets that help identify equity gaps and bright spots · Produce reports, briefs, data visualizations, blogs, and other resources to further inform policymakers, educators, journalists, and other public audiences of Ed Trust - New York’s agenda. · Serve as a spokesperson for Ed Trust - New York by sharing and elevating analyses and policy recommendations publicly with various audiences--including the media, advocates, and policymakers -- that inform and align with Ed Trust’s policy priorities of eliminating educational disparities and enhancing student outcomes. · Elevate Ed Trust’s policy priorities by developing key relationships and representing the organization in external meetings with external stakeholders, peer organizations, policymakers, leaders, funders, and other advocates. · Collaborate internally across EdTrust - New York to support fundraising and grants management, strategic communications · Support and facilitate advisory groups that inform EdTrust - New York’s strategic actions and research products, including topical advisory groups that include student members · Respond to rapid response inquiries about policy and/or data analyses from staff, as well as work with the team to respond to policymakers, advocates, the media, and the public IDEAL SKILLS AND CHARACTERISTICS · Shared belief in Ed Trust’s mission and a commitment to improving educational equity with a focus on racial equity · Dedication in contributing to and maintaining an equitable working environment · Excellent analytic and communication skills, both oral and written, and in a variety of formats and contexts · Strong project management (including time management) skills, with the ability to manage work across multiple stakeholders and meet project milestones / deadlines · Advanced knowledge and experience in Excel, R/R Studio, Tableau, Python, SQL and github; · Knowledge and experience in Excel, ASANA, Microsoft Outlook, and other administrative software · Demonstrated ability to manage and manipulate data and conduct descriptive analyses with excellence · Critical thinker, problem solver, and continuous learner, with ability and interest in working in a fast-paced and collaborative office · Willingness to receive and act upon, as well as provide, constructive feedback QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE The ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experience: · At least a bachelor’s degree in a relevant field; advanced degree a plus/preferred? · At least four years of experience conducting and/or analyzing research and data in education policy or a related field, preferably on topics of equity · Demonstrated ability to produce quantitative and qualitative research analyses that address education equity and closing gaps in opportunity and outcomes · Significant understanding of education policy in New York City / New York State, and the ability to learn, understand and apply relevant qualitative and quantitative education data to a policy context · Knowledge of and familiarity with publicly available data sources on P12 education in New York City / New York State · Demonstrated experience using analytical software and coding COMPENSATION This position falls in Level C of our salary structure. jobs.title: Senior Research Data Analyst – Prenatal-to-3 Policy Impact Center
jobs.description: Senior Research Data Analyst – Prenatal-to-3 Policy Impact Center Job Description Summary: The Prenatal-to-3 Policy Impact Center aims to accelerate states’ implementation of evidence-based policies that help all children thrive from the start. We seek an experienced Senior Research Data Analyst to provide data management and analysis expertise to projects across the Center. The role primarily includes original survey and program data cleaning, data management, and statistical analyses for a portfolio of original research and evaluation projects. The Policy Impact Center’s research seeks to build the evidence base in key areas related to the impact of state policies and programs on outcomes for infants, toddlers, and their families. The role of the Senior Research Data Analyst is essential for transforming raw data into research assets, ensuring the validity and credibility of the Center’s research, resolving complex data challenges, and supporting timely research-based deliverables. This Senior Research Data Analyst position provides essential data expertise and rigorous analytic support and guidance to a team of data researchers responsible for supporting the Center’s goals to build the evidence base for effective and equitable policymaking, track state progress in building a more effective and equitable system of care, and shape policy development in states through targeted assistance and support. General Notes: This position is a term appointment for 12 months beginning upon date of hire, and reports functionally and administratively to the Director of Data and Analytics, Kels Bowman. Applicants from underrepresented groups are encouraged to apply. We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse environment to continue to build a strong and equitable prenatal-to-3 system of care. This position can be performed remotely, and hybrid remote-work opportunities are available. Visa sponsorship is unavailable for this position. Coding Test Requirement: As part of the selection process, competitive candidates will be asked to complete a 2-hour coding test. This test will assess your proficiency in coding, analyzing, and interpreting data. To complete the exercise, candidates will need access to a computer with R software. The primary responsibilities of the position include: Data management, analysis, research, and writing: Contribute to the development of research questions, study designs, analytic plans, and methodological approaches for original research and evaluation projects Manage survey data cleaning and preparation, including guiding processes for data collection and testing, providing support in developing the analytic plan and analysis timeline, implementing quality assurance protocols and detailed documentation, constructing clean, validated analytic datasets that serve as the foundation for the Center’s portfolio of original research Contribute to the development, programming, testing, and refinement of surveys, including reviewing measures, response options, skip logic, and data structures to ensure alignment with research questions and analytic plans Work independently with messy, real-world data and exercise judgment in resolving data quality issues, missing data, and documentation challenges, ensuring analytic datasets are defensible Acquire, manage, and analyze raw datasets, including administrative data from state agencies and national longitudinal sources such as Census, with demonstrated ability to merge datasets, clean and prepare data for analysis, and assess representativeness, processes essential to the Center’s research goals Interpret data and independently select and apply appropriate statistical tests, analyze results, and provide ongoing reports Contribute to and/or lead the production of written products and academic publications translating the results of policy research and analyses into actionable insights for stakeholders and state policymakers. Project management and leadership: Ensure the methodological quality, validity, and integrity of all research analyses conducted, considering the most rigorous possible analytic approaches, appropriate assumptions and interpretation, and careful documentation Communicate effectively with key project staff to ensure they are appropriately informed of project progress, key decisions, and emerging issues Take a leadership role in managing data processes including data collection, management, and analysis Monitor compliance with data security and data retention policies to maintain and ensure the integrity of the Center’s data and research Coordinate with clients and stakeholders, as necessary to obtain and manage administrative datasets Contribute to developing and improving processes and procedures Mentor and train staff in survey data cleaning, analytic workflows, and team processes Monitor and supervise students to effectively contribute to projects Supervisory Relationships: This position may supervise students and does not have staff supervisory responsibility. Required/Essential qualifications: Exceptional interpersonal skills and an ability to work collaboratively with others in a team environment Experience conducting data management, cleaning, and analysis using original survey data Strong skills in R Exceptional analytic and critical thinking skills Excellent project management and organizational skills, strong problem-solving abilities, tenacity about details and organization Strong written communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex concepts clearly and concisely Experience contributing to original research or program evaluation projects, including developing analytic plans, documenting methods, and interpreting findings Ability to come up to speed on new topics quickly, multi-task effectively, and produce high-quality work under time constraints; flexible and able to adapt to changing timelines and circumstances when needed Demonstrated understanding and support for key concepts in diversity, equity, and inclusion Demonstrated commitment to valuing diversity and contributing to an inclusive working and learning environment Master’s degree with major coursework in the field of assignment, plus at least three years of related experience; Additional related experience may substitute for required education Preferred skills: Experience providing supervision and guidance to other staff Skills in Stata Graduate-level coursework or applied experience in research methods, survey methodology, program evaluation, causal inference, or applied statistics Experience with survey data tools (e.g., REDCap, Qualtrics) Knowledge of and familiarity with topics related to early childhood and/or social policy Commitment to Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion At Vanderbilt University, we are intentional about and assume accountability for fostering advancement and respect for equity, diversity, and inclusion for all students, faculty, and staff. Our commitment to diversity makes us who we are. We have created a community that celebrates differences and lets individuality thrive. As part of this commitment, we actively value diversity in our workplace and learning environments as we seek to take advantage of the rich backgrounds and abilities of everyone. The diverse voices of Vanderbilt represent an invaluable resource for the University in its efforts to fulfill its mission and strive to be an example of excellence in higher education. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law. least one video project are required for this position.
