jobs.title: Instructional Designer
jobs.description: Instructional Designer Fully Remote Description SUMMARY: The Instructional Designer - Learning Experience Design assesses learning needs and designs, develops, and delivers innovative learning solutions aligned with organizational goals, learner competencies, and regulatory requirements across multiple content domains and modality channels. The position includes hands-on development. The instructional designer completes projects from discovery through evaluation and supports ongoing curriculum management, content governance, and learning quality standards. Reporting to the Instructional Design Director, this position operates independently and collaborates with subject matter experts, program partners, and team members to turn complex information into practical, accessible learning resources across behavioral health, training, and organizational development initiatives. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include but are not limited to: Assess learner and performance needs and recommend appropriate solutions in collaboration with the Instructional Design Director and program partners. Gather, clarify, and translate complex technical, clinical, and regulatory content into plain-language learning materials and practical guidance, preserving the intended meaning and validating accuracy with appropriate subject matter experts. Conduct audience analysis and adapt content, terminology, examples, and learning approaches to learners’ roles, prior knowledge, work settings, and application needs; organize content into logical learning pathways and sequences. Develop learning objectives, instructional approaches, storyboards, activities, and assessments aligned with established content standards and learner needs. Create learning blueprints and, when projects are handed off, complete design packages for developers; remain available to review the product against the blueprint. Build eLearning modules, instructor-led training materials, facilitation guides, scripts, videos, job aids, webinars, and blended learning solutions using appropriate authoring tools. Prepare and test courses for LMS delivery, including SCORM packaging. Apply department standards for instructional quality, accessibility, usability, and visual consistency. Coordinate project responsibilities, reviews, and timelines with the Director and team members. Design evaluation measures and feedback mechanisms in partnership with Evaluation/Analytics team members and use data to refine and improve learning solutions. Support curriculum planning, content governance across the LMS, EHR knowledge base, and agency websites. Develop and maintain learning management system (LMS) documentation, templates, and best practices guides. Conduct instructional design reviews and quality assurance checks on learning materials to ensure adherence to standards. Support training and mentoring of new design team members or contractors on ID processes and tools. Stay current with instructional design best practices, emerging technologies, and industry trends through ongoing professional development. Other duties as assigned, demonstrating flexibility and commitment to organizational success. QUALIFICATIONS – An acceptable equivalent combination of education, experience, and skill may be considered. Education: Bachelor's degree in Instructional Design, Education, Learning Sciences, Human Resources, Communications, or a related field. Experience: Four (4) or more years of experience in instructional design, learning and development, training design, or related field. Demonstrated experience designing healthcare, compliance, behavioral health, or regulatory training materials. Experience with learning management systems (LMS) administration, course configuration and learning paths. Experience designing and delivering training across multiple modalities: eLearning, instructor-led, synchronous, asynchronous, and blended formats. Demonstrated experience with video production, editing, and multimedia content creation. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Job Specific Knowledge & Skills: Proficiency in eLearning authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline, Rise, or Captivate; ability to quickly master new authoring platforms. Working knowledge of SCORM standards. Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel) and learning management systems. Strong working knowledge of Section 508 and WCAG accessibility standards for digital content. Experience with video production tools such as Camtasia, Adobe Premiere Pro, or similar. Proficiency with visual design and graphic design software such as Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, or equivalent. Demonstrated ability to apply adult learning principles and instructional design models to practical learning outcomes. Strong SME collaboration, content synthesis, writing, and plain-language communication skills. Communication Collaboration & Time Management Skills: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with excellent written and verbal communication abilities. Ability to explain complex learning and instructional design concepts clearly to subject matter experts, leaders, and diverse audiences. Ability to exercise independent judgment, conduct research, and ask appropriate probing questions to complete necessary tasks. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously with varying priority levels and competing deadlines. Comfortable using virtual collaboration tools, including Teams, Zoom, and SharePoint. Personal Attributes: Detail-oriented and organized, with a strong commitment to accuracy, quality, and best practices. Demonstrates quality assurance mindset with excellent attention to detail and commitment to accuracy in all work products. Demonstrates initiative, independence, sound judgment, and resourcefulness in completing assignments. Adaptable and able to manage shifting priorities in a fast-paced, evolving learning environment. Comfortable working in a remote environment and maintaining accountability to leadership. PHYSICAL DEMANDS - The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit and stand; use phone and headset; use hands, arms, and fingers to type; answer phones; write; use a calculator; lift and carry materials weighing up to 10 pounds; demonstrate clear vision to read printed materials and a computer screen; use hearing and speech to communicate in person and over the telephone; and drive a motor vehicle on public roads and highways. SENSORY DEMANDS - The incumbent must spend long hours in intense concentration. The incumbent must also spend long hours on the computer entering information, which requires attention to detail and high levels of accuracy. MENTAL DEMANDS - There are a number of deadlines associated with this position, which may cause significant pressure. The incumbent must also deal with a wide variety of people on various issues and manage multiple concurrent projects and shifting priorities in a fast-paced, high-stakes environment. REGULAR WORK SCHEDULE – Varies depending on business needs; however, company normal business hours are 8:00am to 5:00pm, Monday – Friday Salary Description $110,000 - $135,000

jobs.title: Health Analyst
jobs.description: The Health Analysis Division (HAD) seeks an analyst to model the effects of health policies and prepare technical information, reports, and testimony for Congress. The division is developing modeling capacity across a range of health policy areas, including health insurance markets and enrollment, cost sharing in Medicare, long-term care, and prescription drug prices and spending (for example, price negotiation in Medicare Part D). Applicants must have a Ph.D. in biostatistics, data science, economics, health economics, health policy, public policy, statistics, or a related discipline, or a master's degree in one of those disciplines with a quantitative focus and at least three years of relevant experience. That experience may include health policy analysis or applied statistical modeling or forecasting. Applicants should have an interest in the development of policy-relevant models, strong quantitative skills, experience with large-scale data and reproducible workflows, and an in-depth knowledge of at least one programming language (with a preference for Python or R). jobs.title: Weapons and Nuclear Weapons/Missile Defense Analyst
jobs.description: The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) is a small, nonpartisan agency that provides economic, budgetary, and policy analysis to Congress. CBO's National Security Division seeks analysts to conduct studies of the costs and capabilities of defense systems and potential acquisition programs, including conventional weapons, military aviation, space systems, command, control, and communications (C3) systems, nuclear forces, and air and missile defense programs. Qualifications: Candidates must have a graduate degree or equivalent experience in physical sciences, engineering, operations research, statistics, applied mathematics, national security policy, public policy, or a related field. All candidates must have demonstrated experience in quantitative analysis. The ideal candidate will have experience in one or more of the following areas: weapons systems analysis, military aviation, space systems, nuclear weapons systems, air and missile defense, defense budget analysis, program cost analysis, operations research, or analyses of alternatives. CBO is seeking candidates at two experience levels: Analyst: At least three years of relevant experience, which may include graduate work. Experienced Analyst: At least five years of work experience, including experience working independently. Leadership of analytical studies or tasks within larger studies is desirable, and a demonstrated record of professional publications is highly desirable. CBO analyses are often conducted by a single analyst or a small team. Candidates must be able to develop models that capture the principal factors driving costs or affecting capabilities, often when data are limited. CBO maintains high standards for accuracy, precision, clarity, and objectivity. Candidates must be excellent writers who can make complex technical topics understandable to nonexpert audiences. The ability to work with Congressional staff and develop relationships with experts in government, think tanks, and private industry is also important. Candidates must have or be able to obtain and maintain a Top Secret security clearance. Work Schedule: This position follows a hybrid work schedule requiring employees to work in person at CBO's Washington, D.C., offices on designated core days. Additional in-office days may be required depending on operational needs. Full-time telework is not available.

BASIC REQUIREMENT OR INDIVIDUAL OCCUPATIONAL REQUIREMENT: Degree: Physical science, engineering, or mathematics that included 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science such as mechanics, dynamics, properties of materials, and electronics. OR Combination of education and experience -- education equivalent to one of the majors shown in A above that included at least 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science, plus appropriate experience or additional education. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below. FOR GS-11: Successfully completed 1 year of specialized experience that equipped the applicant with the particular knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position, and that is typically in or related to the position to be filled. To be creditable, the specialized experience must have been at the GS-09 grade level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service. Examples of specialized experience may include: serving as an advanced analyst in the field of analytical chemistry for analysis of water samples (primarily stream water, soil leachate, and precipitation); using equipment and instruments including atomic absorption spectrophotometers, ion chromatographs, automatic titrators, ammonia analyzers, carbon analyzers, and nitrogen analyzers; performing preparations, quality control, calibrations, calculations, waste and sample disposal related to the analysis; training other technicians in the performance of routine duties; and generating reports based on analytical data produced. FOR GS-12: Successfully completed 1 year of specialized experience that equipped the applicant with the particular knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position, and that is in or related to the position to be filled. To be creditable, the specialized experience must have been at the GS-11 grade level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service. Examples of creditable specialized experience may include planning and executing complex physical science studies, which usually involved intensive investigations into recognized phenomena. This work typically involved conventional methods and techniques though it required going beyond clear precedents, and required adapting methods to the problems at hand and interpreting findings in terms of their scientific significance. At this level, physical scientists have the ability to independently perform scientific work of considerable difficulty. FOR GS-13: Successfully completed 1 year of specialized experience that equipped the applicant with the particular knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position, and that is in or related to the position to be filled. To be creditable, the specialized experience must have been at the GS-12 grade level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service. Examples may include research design; analysis and implementation; analysis and/or consolidation of research findings data to identify strategic research areas or needs. FOR GS-14: Successfully completed 1 year of specialized experience that equipped the applicant with the particular knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position, and that is in or related to the position to be filled. To be creditable, the specialized experience must have been at the GS-13 grade level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service. Examples may include providing research and science support information for program policy or Regional program management of complex or interdisciplinary nature; identifying developmental and training needs of managers to address program area design challenges and making policy or programmatic recommendations for specific developmental tasking and training assignments; participating in policy and guidance development to enable organizational implementation of policy or program initiatives; monitoring program implementation and making recommendations on the allocation of resources; adjustment of organizational engagement methods, protocols or procedures to ensure maximum effectiveness, efficiency, and economy. FOR GS-15: Successfully completed 1 year of specialized experience that equipped the applicant with the particular knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position, and that is in or related to the position to be filled. To be creditable, the specialized experience must have been at the GS-14 grade level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service. Examples of creditable specialized experience: performs management planning duties such as concept development, master integration planning, and programming design for programs or projects, taking into account feasibility, costs, and economics; conceives, plans, conducts and reviews work in areas where there is little theory to guide efforts; Leads a research group and/or project; Performs environmental modeling and forecasting duties; Publishes research findings in scientific journals and Represents the organization to larger scientific and management groups. To view qualifying educational requirements and/or combination of education and experience, click on the following link: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/1300/general-physical-science-series-1301/ KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of professional environmental physical scientific principles, practices, techniques, and procedures to effectively participate in project development, execution, training, and assistance in assigned projects (see Environmental Program Checklist). Knowledge to troubleshoot routine environmental physical science problems requiring investigation of unsanitary or questionable conditions in assigned projects (see Environmental Program Checklist). Knowledge of applicable Federal, State, and local laws, regulations, and other guidance to make decisions and recommendations concerning assigned restoration, compliance, conservation, pollution prevention and/or integration principles and practices. Skill to integrate an interdisciplinary team of professionals to include attorneys, public health specialists, public affairs specialists, biological scientists, environmental engineers, physical scientists, general engineers, community planners, regulators, other governmental officials, and community groups. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

jobs.title: FinOps Analyst -Remote - US
jobs.description: About Ellucian Ellucian powers innovation for higher education, partnering with approximately 3,000 customers across 50 countries, serving more than 21 million students. Ellucian's AI-powered platform, trained on the richest dataset available in higher education, drives efficiency, personalized experiences, and strengthened engagement for all students, faculty and staff. Fueled by decades of experience with a singular focus on the unique needs of learning institutions, the Ellucian platform features best-in-class SaaS capabilities and delivers insights needed now and into the future. These solutions and services span the entire student lifecycle, including data-rich tools for student recruitment, enrollment, and retention to workforce analytics, fundraising, and alumni engagement. Ellucian's innovative solutions, vast ecosystem of partners and user community of more than 45,000 provides best practices leading to greater institutional success and achieving better student outcomes. About the Opportunity At Ellucian, we believe in the transformative power of education, and our cloud solutions are central to powering that transformation for colleges and universities around the world. The FinOps team supports the development, scalability, and financial sustainability of Ellucian's cloud solutions through effective governance, financial transparency, and cross-functional collaboration. The team helps establish organizational accountability for technology consumption and costs while maximizing the business value of cloud and other consumption-based technology investments. Success is measured through predictable and scalable costs, effective governance, improved financial visibility, and measurable optimization outcomes. As a FinOps Analyst, you will help drive financial accountability, governance, and optimization across Ellucian's cloud and technology investments. You will independently own assigned FinOps initiatives, analyze technology consumption and spending, identify opportunities for improvement, and partner with technical and business stakeholders to translate financial and operational data into actionable decisions. Where You Will Make an Impact Own and drive FinOps initiatives within assigned areas of responsibility, improving visibility, accountability, governance, and optimization across cloud and technology consumption and spend. Analyze cloud and third-party technology usage, cost, and operational data to identify trends, anomalies, cost drivers, financial risks, and opportunities for optimization. Identify, quantify, prioritize, and track cost optimization opportunities, partnering with technology owners and stakeholders to implement improvements and measure realized savings, cost avoidance, and business value. Support and improve FinOps governance practices, including resource tagging, metadata standards, cost allocation, ownership, policy compliance, and controls that enable accurate financial accountability. Monitor consumption-based technology platforms and services, including Datadog, to understand usage patterns, evaluate cost drivers, forecast financial impact, and identify opportunities to improve efficiency and value. Develop and maintain dashboards, reports, forecasts, and key performance indicators that provide visibility into technology consumption, optimization progress, governance compliance, and financial performance. Support budgeting and forecasting activities by analyzing historical consumption, growth trends, business drivers, and planned technology changes to improve financial predictability. Utilize cloud financial management, observability, analytics, and FinOps tools to support operational requirements, financial analysis, and technology optimization initiatives. Partner with stakeholders across Cloud Engineering/Operations, R&D, Product, Finance, Procurement, and other business functions to integrate FinOps practices into day-to-day technology planning and decision-making. Investigate unexpected consumption or cost changes, collaborating with technical teams to identify contributing factors, assess financial impact, and recommend appropriate corrective actions. Help evaluate and establish financial governance for emerging technologies and consumption models, including SaaS, observability, data platforms, and AI services as organizational needs evolve. Identify opportunities to improve FinOps processes, controls, reporting, and operational effectiveness through automation, improved analytics, and standardized practices. Support improvements in automated reporting, consumption monitoring, and cost anomaly detection to increase efficiency, data accuracy, and visibility into optimization opportunities. Contribute to the continued maturity of FinOps practices by improving cost allocation, forecasting, governance, and financial accountability across technology investments. What You Will Bring 2+ years of experience in FinOps, cloud financial management, cloud operations, observability/platform operations, technology governance, technical program/project management, financial/business analysis, or a related discipline. Hands-on experience with Datadog, including the ability to analyze usage, consumption trends, and cost drivers across one or more Datadog capabilities. Experience analyzing technology usage and cost data to identify trends, anomalies, optimization opportunities, and financial impact. Experience supporting or implementing technology governance practices such as resource tagging, metadata management, cost allocation, policy compliance, or ownership and accountability controls. Working knowledge of public cloud infrastructure and services, with AWS experience particularly relevant. Experience developing dashboards, reports, and analytical views used to communicate financial or operational performance, including consumption trends, forecasting, and optimization opportunities. Strong Microsoft Excel and data analysis skills, with the ability to work with complex datasets and translate findings into actionable recommendations. Familiarity with cloud financial management and analytics tools such as Cloudability, AWS Cost Explorer, Cost and Usage Reports (CUR), CUDOS, or similar platforms. Understanding of consumption-based technology cost models, including cloud infrastructure, SaaS, observability platforms, or other variable-consumption services. Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate cost drivers, evaluate opportunities, and recommend practical solutions. Ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders and influence action without direct authority. Ability to independently manage assigned initiatives and priorities while collaborating effectively across technical and business teams. Detail-oriented, with strong documentation, organizational, and financial reporting skills. Familiarity with FinOps principles, technology cost optimization, and opportunities to improve reporting or governance through automation and analytics. Experience using AI-powered productivity tools, such as ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, or similar solutions, to support data analysis, research, reporting, documentation, and workflow efficiency, with appropriate validation of AI-generated outputs. Develop visual process aids, such as flowcharts, decision trees, and swim lane diagrams to supplement written procedures and training materials. jobs.title: Atlassian Instructional Designer Level III
jobs.description: Overview: LMI is seeking an Instructional Designer at the Level III level to develop accessible, effective learning experiences supporting Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Agile practices and Atlassian Cloud adoption. This role combines learning strategy, curriculum design, digital content development, and performance support to translate complex processes and tools into practical instruction for a diverse federal workforce. The Instructional Designer will design role-based learning paths for leadership, Scrum Masters, Product Owners, delivery teams, and tool administrators. The position develops live-instruction materials, self-paced e-learning, hands-on exercises, job aids, assessments, and adoption-hub resources using ADDIE or SAM and tools such as Articulate Storyline and Rise. Content will be prepared for the existing learning management system and validated against accessibility requirements. This is not a slide-production-only role. The designer must identify the performance problem behind a training request, define measurable learning objectives, test content with representative learners, and refine materials based on completion data and user feedback. The ideal candidate balances technical accuracy with adult-learning principles, concise writing, visual clarity, and Section 508 compliance. LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed. Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government, efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, healthcare, and energy sectors—helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value. Responsibilities: Conduct needs analysis and translate assessed learner cohorts and job roles into measurable learning objectives. Design role-based courses on Agile practices, Jira Cloud, reporting, and administrative workflows using ADDIE or SAM. Develop instructor guides, presentations, demonstrations, exercises, assessments, e-learning modules, and concise job aids. Author and maintain Articulate Storyline or Rise content and package courses for SCORM-compatible LMS delivery. Coordinate publishing, course metadata, completion tracking, pilot testing, and revisions with LMS and training operations staff. Perform accessibility reviews and coordinate Section 508 and WCAG testing and remediation for self-paced content. Maintain consistent, version-controlled adoption-hub and knowledge-base resources. Create curriculum maps that connect learner role and readiness level to objectives, prerequisites, modality, activities, practice tasks, and knowledge checks. Script accurate Jira Cloud and Agile demonstrations with consistent terminology, realistic workflows, annotated screenshots, and accessible interaction patterns. Build facilitator notes, learner guides, scenario-based exercises, quick-reference cards, and assessment items that reinforce on-the-job application. Conduct editorial, functional, and accessibility quality assurance; document remediation decisions before course publication and updates. Manage content versions, review cycles, SME approvals, and content ownership so learning materials stay aligned with changing platform configurations. Qualifications: Required: Bachelor's degree in instructional design, education, learning technologies, educational psychology, or a related field. 3+ years of instructional design, e-learning development, or performance-support experience. Demonstrated use of ADDIE or SAM and Articulate Storyline or Rise. Experience with SCORM packages, LMS course publishing, and training evaluation. Knowledge of Section 508 and WCAG accessibility requirements and accessible content design. Ability to obtain and maintain a favorable Public Trust determination and satisfy applicable federal personnel vetting, security, privacy, accessibility, and data-handling requirements. Section 508 Trusted Tester certification or equivalent formal accessibility testing credential. Portfolio or work samples demonstrating both instructor-led design and interactive e-learning or digital performance support. Ability to collaborate with technical SMEs and translate detailed workflows into accurate, concise, and accessible learner-facing content. Desired: Prior experience supporting the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), or federal health programs is highly desirable. Master's degree in instructional design, education, learning technologies, or a related discipline. Agile, Jira Cloud, Confluence Cloud, or federal enterprise training experience. Experience creating blended learning for large distributed audiences. Experience designing simulation-based software instruction, formative assessments, and post-training performance reinforcement. Additional certifications such as ATD Associate Professional in Talent Development (APTD) or Certified Professional in Talent Development (CPTD) are desirable. Target Salary Range: $85,000 - $115,000 Disclaimer: The salary range displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is not a guarantee of compensation. jobs.title: Instructional Designer - Tysons, VA
jobs.description: Overview: About M.C. Dean M.C. Dean is Building Intelligence®. We design, build, operate, and maintain cyber-physical solutions for the nation’s most recognizable mission critical facilities, secure environments, complex infrastructure, and global enterprises. The company’s capabilities include electrical power systems, electronic security, telecommunications, life safety, automation and controls, audio visual, and IT systems. M.C. Dean is headquartered in Tysons, Virginia and employs more than 9,000 professionals who engineer and deploy automated, secure, and resilient power and technology systems; and deliver the management platforms essential for long-term system sustainability. Why Join Us? Our people are passionate about engineering innovation that improves lives and drives impactful change. Guided by our core values—agility, expertise, and trust—we foster a collaborative and forward-thinking work environment. At M.C. Dean, we are committed to building the next generation of technical leaders in electrical, engineering, and cybersecurity industries. Position Summary The Instructional Designer designs, develops, and maintains high-quality learning solutions that support M.C. Dean’s technical, operational, and leadership development needs. This role translates complex subject matter and business requirements into practical, engaging, and measurable learning experiences delivered through eLearning, instructor-led training, blended learning, and on-the-job training. Working with subject matter experts, business unit leaders, and the Content Development Manager, the Instructional Designer develops scalable learning products aligned to instructional design standards, career-framework competencies, and workforce performance requirements. Responsibilities: Core Expectations This role requires initiative, independent judgment, accountability, and a commitment to practical, measurable improvements. Key expectations include: Independently manages assigned projects from analysis through development, testing, and delivery. Translates complex technical or operational information into clear, accurate learning experiences. Proactively identifies instructional gaps and recommends appropriate solutions. Builds productive SME and stakeholder relationships to validate accuracy and maintain momentum. Applies established standards while improving quality, efficiency, and learner engagement. Takes accountability for quality, timelines, and timely resolution of feedback. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Instructional Design and Development: Design eLearning, instructor-led, blended, job aids, assessments, and other materials using adult learning principles. Learning Needs Analysis: Work with SMEs and stakeholders to identify performance gaps, objectives, learner needs, and instructional solutions. Curriculum Development: Translate technical, operational, and leadership content into structured learning experiences that build job-specific competencies. Career Framework Alignment: Develop learning products aligned to approved pathways, competency requirements, and development needs. Technical Content Development: Collaborate with SMEs on field operations, manufacturing, engineering, commissioning, safety-related processes, and other disciplines. Leadership Development Content: Design facilitator guides, participant resources, case studies, and activities for leadership programs. SME Knowledge Conversion: Transform SME-led training, presentations, procedures, and pilots into standardized, repeatable products. Assessment Development: Create knowledge checks, practical assessments, proficiency evaluations, and tools to validate competency. On-the-Job Learning: Develop OJT guides, task checklists, observation tools, and supervisor resources. Content Quality Assurance: Apply templates, accessibility and editorial standards, and quality reviews; incorporate feedback before publishing. Learning Technology Coordination: Develop content using approved tools and prepare materials for technical review, packaging, and publication by Learning Technology. Project Management: Manage schedules, SME reviews, status communication, and risks affecting delivery. Evaluation and Continuous Improvement: Review learner feedback, assessment results, and performance data to improve content. Supervisory Responsibilities No direct supervisory responsibilities. May provide project guidance, peer reviews, or support to other instructional designers and external development resources as assigned. Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree required. Experience Requirements 2+ years of experience in instructional design, curriculum development, or learning content development. Experience designing instructor-led, eLearning, and blended learning solutions. Experience using instructional design methodologies and adult learning principles to create measurable outcomes. Proficiency with authoring tools such as Articulate 360, Storyline, Rise, Vyond, or comparable applications. Graphic design experience preferred, including the ability to apply visual design principles, typography, layout, and multimedia elements to create engaging, professional learning materials across digital and instructor-led formats. Experience developing complex or technical information with SMEs. Experience developing assessments, facilitator guides, job aids, and instructional resources. Experience with technical, engineering, construction, manufacturing, or operational workforces preferred. Familiarity with LMS platforms and SCORM/xAPI preferred. Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Strong instructional design, adult learning, and assessment knowledge. Ability to simplify technical information without compromising accuracy. Strong writing, editing, visual design, and organization skills. Proficiency with digital authoring, multimedia, and Microsoft Office tools. Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines. Strong communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills. Ability to incorporate feedback and apply quality standards. Working knowledge of accessibility and digital learning best practices. Working Conditions & Physical Demands Office-based position with occasional travel to manufacturing facilities, project sites, training locations, and other business unit operations for needs analysis, SME collaboration, and observations. Field site safety requirements apply. We offer an excellent benefits package including: A competitive salary Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance Paid time off Tuition reimbursement 401k Retirement Plan Military Reserve pay offset Paid maternity leave Abilities: Exposure to computer screens for an extended period of time. Sitting for extended periods of time. Reach by extending hands or arms in any direction. Have finger dexterity in order to manipulate objects with fingers rather than whole hands or arms, for example, using a keyboard. Listen to and understand information and ideas presented through spoken words and sentences. Communicate information and ideas in speaking so others will understand. Read and understand information and ideas presented in writing. Apply general rules to specific problems to produce answers that make sense. Identify and understand the speech of another person. Pay Range: USD $78,320.00 - USD $97,900.00 /Yr.

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist
jobs.description: The position of Senior Data Scientist, is in the Office of the Administrator at the National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS), U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA). Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. Any resume that exceeds the maximum length of two (2) pages will be removed from consideration. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position. Failure to meet the basic qualification requirement and address all Technical Qualification factors within your resume will result in your application being disqualified. There is NO requirement to prepare a narrative statement specifically addressing the Technical Qualifications (TQs). The Mandatory Technical Qualifications are listed below. Typically, experience of this nature will have been gained at or above the GS-14/15 grade level in the federal service or its equivalent in the private sector. Applicants must clearly demonstrate in their resume that they meet the following technical qualification(s). Failure to meet basic qualification requirements and to submit narratives for the Mandatory Technical Qualification factors will automatically disqualify an applicant. 1. TQ1 - Demonstrated expert-level experience applying data science, machine learning, statistical computing, predictive modeling, geospatial analytics, and related advanced methods to large-scale statistical or data-production programs. Experience must include leading the development or operational implementation of data-driven solutions involving multiple data sources such as survey, census, administrative, remotely sensed, or other alternative data to improve the quality, timeliness, efficiency, or relevance of official statistics. The applicant must demonstrate the ability to evaluate emerging technologies and convert advanced data-science methods into secure, reliable, reproducible, and scalable production capabilities. TQ2 - Enterprise Data-Science Modernization and Technical Governance - Demonstrated experience serving as a senior technical authority and leading enterprise-scale modernization of data-science, analytical, or statistical-production environments. Experience must include establishing technical standards and governance for data interoperability, analytical infrastructure, data engineering, model lifecycle management, and statistical quality; advising senior executives on modernization strategies, risks, and investment priorities; and leading multidisciplinary initiatives across organizational boundaries. The applicant must demonstrate accomplishments that produced measurable improvements in the delivery of mission-critical statistical products, strengthened organizational data-science capabilities, or advanced the use of innovative methods within a federal statistical or similarly complex operational environment. Time in grade requirements does not apply to SL positions. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs {e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations {e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Applicants must meet all qualifications and eligibility (including educational) requirements by the closing date of the announcement.

jobs.title: Data Scientist Development Program (DSDP) - Entry to Expert Level
jobs.description: Data science is present in every aspect of NSA's mission to protect the nation. By joining our team, you will tackle challenging problems by leveraging big data, high-performance computing, machine learning and more. We are looking for senior-level data scientists who believe that answers to hard questions lie in the yet-to-be-told story of diverse, complicated data sets. Qualifications: The qualifications listed are the minimum acceptable to be considered for the position. Applicants will be asked to complete the Data Science Examination (DSE) which evaluates their knowledge of statistics, mathematics, and computer science topics that pertain to data science work. Passing this examination at a local testing site is a requirement in order to be considered for selection into a data scientist position. Upon passing the examination, applicants will be evaluated for the minimum qualifications outlined in this ad. Transcripts for each academic institution are required prior to being invited to interview with Agency data science professionals and should be submitted as part of the online application. Unofficial transcripts are fine at this stage. ENTRY Entry is with an Associate's degree plus 2 years of relevant experience, or a Bachelor's degree and no experience, or a Master's degree and no experience. Relevant experience must be in one or more of the following: designing/implementing machine learning, data mining, statistical analysis, statistical consulting, super intelligence development, computational science, software engineering, technical writing, data visualization, or data engineering. FULL PERFORMANCE Entry is with an Associate's degree plus 5 years of relevant experience, or a Bachelor's degree plus 3 years of relevant experience, or a Master's degree plus 1 year of relevant experience, or a Doctoral degree and no experience. Experience must include both programming and one or more of the following: designing/implementing machine learning, data mining, statistical analysis, statistical consulting, super intelligence development, computational science, technical writing, data visualization, or data engineering. SENIOR Entry is with an Associate's degree plus 8 years of relevant experience, or a Bachelor's degree plus 6 years of relevant experience, or a Master's degree plus 4 years of relevant experience, or a Doctoral degree plus 2 years of relevant experience. Experience must include both programming and one or more of the following: designing/implementing machine learning, data mining, statistical analysis, statistical consulting, super intelligence development, computational science, technical writing, data visualization, or data engineering. Experience must also include formal or informal leadership. EXPERT Entry is with an Associate's degree plus 11 years of relevant experience, or a Bachelor's degree plus 9 years of relevant experience, or a Master's degree plus 7 years of relevant experience, or a Doctoral degree plus 5 years of relevant experience. Experience must include both programming and one or more of the following: designing/implementing machine learning, data mining, statistical analysis, statistical consulting, super intelligence development, computational science, technical writing, data visualization, or data engineering. Experience must also include formal or informal leadership.

jobs.title: Interdisciplinary (Transportation Research Analyst) Direct-Hire
jobs.description: This position is located in the Safety Research Division, Office of Research and Engineering, National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB). The incumbent serves as an Interdisciplinary General Engineer / Data Scientist / Statistician who plans and conducts transportation safety studies and evaluations of the effectiveness of transportation safety programs and countermeasures. Qualifications: To be eligible for this position, applicants must meet the Basic Qualification Requirements outlined below, as well as the Individual Occupational Requirements (IOR) specified in the Education section of this announcement for the applicable occupational series for which they wish to be considered. GS-11 One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-9 grade level in the Federal Service. Specialized experience is experience assisting with research studies by performing literature searches and reviews in transportation safety, injury prevention, or a closely related safety field; experience collecting, organizing, cleaning, and validating datasets, and conducting statistical analyses using Python or R or SQL under the guidance of senior researchers, engineers, data scientists, or statisticians; and experience contributing to written reports, data summaries, or presentations that effectively communicate research findings and key insights to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. OR 3 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a Ph. D. or equivalent doctoral degree. OR a combination of Education and Experience. To be creditable, your education must be directly related to the position being filled. GS-12 One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 in the Federal Service. Experience could have been obtained in the Private sector. Specialized experience is experience contributing to transportation safety research and statistical analyses by applying established study designs, research methodologies, and statistical techniques to defined components of larger research projects such as descriptive studies, systematic and evidence-based reviews, case control studies, or other types of research studies; experience collecting, organizing, and analyzing data using Python and/or R and SQL; and experience using oral and written communication skills to clearly communicate research findings and key insights in plain language to technical and non-technical stakeholders. GS-13 One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 in the Federal Service. Experience could have been obtained in the private sector. Specialized experience is experience conducting independent research and statistical work in transportation safety, applying research study designs, methods, and statistical techniques such as descriptive studies, meta-analyses, systematic or evidence-based reviews, case-control studies, or other types of research studies experience using data science methods and techniques to perform data and statistical analysis using Python and/or R and SQL; and experience using oral and written communication skills to clearly communicate research findings, key insights, and safety recommendations in plain language to technical and non-technical stakeholders. For more information see link: General Engineering Series 0801; Statistics Series 1530; Data Science Series 1560 NOTE: IN DESCRIBING YOUR EXPERIENCE, PLEASE BE CLEAR AND SPECIFIC. WE WILL NOT MAKE ASSUMPTIONS REGARDING YOUR EXPERIENCE. Your resume must clearly show the specialized experience and competencies related to this position. Failure to demonstrate how you possess the education, specialized experience and/or competencies will result in an "Ineligible" rating. GENERAL EDUCATION: All academic degrees and coursework must be completed at an institution that has obtained accreditation or pre-accreditation status from an accrediting body recognized by the U.S. Department of Education for it to be credited towards qualifications. For a list of schools that meet these criteria, see https://www.ed.gov/accreditation?src=rn. Applications submitted without the required supporting documents will not be accepted. An unofficial transcript; statement from the institution's registrar, dean, or other appropriate official; or equivalent documentation is acceptable at the time of application. Education submitted must be appropriately accredited by an accredited body recognized by the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Education. For additional information, refer to the U.S. Department of Education web site at: http://www.ed.gov FOREIGN EDUCATION: If you are using education completed in foreign colleges or universities to meet the qualification requirements, you must show the education credentials have been evaluated by a private organization that specializes in interpretation of foreign education programs and such education has been deemed equivalent to that gained in an accredited U.S. education program; or full credit has been given for the courses at a U.S. accredited college or university. For further information, visit: https://www2.ed.gov/about/offices/list/ous/international/usnei/us/edlite-visitus-forrecog.html

jobs.title: PROGRAM ANALYST

This role requires on-campus presence because the best ideas emerge from real-time collaboration, the mentorship that happens in hallways, and the spontaneous problem-solving that defines startup culture. The Instructional Design Specialist – Emerging Technologies is responsible for designing and developing high-quality online courses while serving as an internal expert in emerging instructional technologies, artificial intelligence, and UX/UI design. This position plays a dual role, contributing directly to course development and leading the exploration, evaluation, and implementation of innovative digital learning solutions. Education and Experience | Master’s degree in Instructional Design, User Experience Design, Education Technology, or a related field. At least 3 years of experience in instructional design. Experience with HTML for basic formatting and accessibility adjustments within LMS environments. Knowledge of instructional design frameworks and models. Experience with eLearning authoring tools (e.g., Articulate Rise, PlayPosit).Demonstrated experience designing and developing online courses, including building content in a Learning Management System (e.g., Blackboard).Experience applying ADA required accessibility standards, adult learning theories, and Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex or technical concepts for non-technical audiences. Demonstrated ability to build and maintain effective professional relationships with faculty, team members, and stakeholders. Skills and Knowledge | Preferred Qualifications: Certification or formal training in UX/UI design. Certification or formal training in AI. Experience developing courses for higher education. Experience in teaching/training. Experience in programming. Responsibilities | Instructional Design & Course Development Facilitate organized, adaptive meetings with faculty to gather information, establish course delivery strategies, and build buy-in for the development process. Define and outline learning objectives, course structure, content delivery methods, assessments, and complementary learning approaches in collaboration with faculty. Articulate and reinforce course development process and clarify faculty responsibilities, as well as establish milestone deadlines, and maintain accountability throughout the project lifecycle. Collaborate closely with faculty and stakeholders to develop course content; maintain strong professional relationships and clear communication throughout the project lifecycle. jobs.description: This vacancy is being filled via the Direct-Hire Authority (DHA) for a Survey Statistician position in the Center for Enterprise Dissemination located in any Federal Statistical Research Data Center within the U.S. Census Bureau. This Job Opportunity Announcement may be used to fill other Survey Statistician, 1530-11/12, FPL GS-12 positions within the Census Bureau in the same geographical location with the same qualifications and specialized experience. Qualifications: Minimum Education Requirement: Degree: that included 15 semester hours in statistics (or in mathematics and statistics, provided at least 6 semester hours were in statistics), and 9 additional semester hours in one or more of the following: physical or biological sciences, medicine, education, or engineering; or in the social sciences including demography, history, economics, social welfare, geography, international relations, social or cultural anthropology, health sociology, political science, public administration, psychology, etc. Credit toward meeting statistical course requirements should be given for courses in which 50 percent of the course content appears to be statistical methods, e.g., courses that included studies in research methods in psychology or economics such as tests and measurements or business cycles, or courses in methods of processing mass statistical data such as tabulating methods or electronic data processing. OR Combination of education and experience -- courses as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. The experience should have included a full range of professional statistical work such as (a) sampling, (b) collecting, computing, and analyzing statistical data, and (c) applying statistical techniques such as measurement of central tendency, dispersion, skewness, sampling error, simple and multiple correlation, analysis of variance, and tests of significance. AND Specialized Experience: For the GS-11, you must have one year of experience at a level of difficulty and responsibility equivalent to the GS-09 in the Federal service. Experience for this position includes: Communicating in-person and in writing to diverse audiences or stakeholders; Applying statistical techniques, methodology, or methods; Assisting developing research plans or conducting research using survey, administrative, or public-use data; Writing reports, papers or presentations that document or summarize research findings. Applicants must demonstrate and provide evidence in at least 3 of the above areas to be qualified. OR Education: 3 years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a Ph.D. degree or Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree. jobs.title: Clinical Lab Scientist
jobs.description: This position is eligible for the Education Debt Reduction Program (EDRP), a student loan payment reimbursement program. You must meet specific individual eligibility requirements in accordance with VHA policy and submit your EDRP application within four months of appointment. Program Approval, award amount (up to $200,000) and eligibility period (one to five years) are determined by the VHA Education Loan Repayment Services program office after complete review of the EDRP application. Qualifications: Applicants pending the completion of educational or certification/licensure requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until all requirements are met. Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. English Language Proficiency: Candidates must be proficient in spoken and written English in accordance with 38 U.S.C. § 7403 (f) Education: A bachelor's degree or higher from an accredited college or university. Foreign Education. To be creditable, education completed outside the U.S. must be deemed at least equivalent to that gained in a conventional U.S. program by a private organization specializing in the interpretation of foreign educational credentials. Graduates of foreign baccalaureate degree programs meet the educational requirements if they meet either of the following: Foreign transcripts are evaluated by an acceptable evaluation agency, and the degree is found to be equivalent to a NAACLS-approved U.S. clinical laboratory science degree program. OR The applicant submits a letter from ASCP BOC or AMT stating the individual is eligible to take the certification examination. NOTE: Possession of a certification identified below automatically determines the foreign education as creditable and no further documentation or proof of equivalency is needed. Certification: Candidates must meet one of the certification options below. Generalist certification as an MLS given by ASCP BOC or AMT. Generalist certification as an MT given by ASCP BOR or AMT. Categorical certification or Specialist certification by ASCP or AMT. NOTE: Categorical and specialist certifications are not acceptable for CLS Generalist positions or lab sections unrelated to the categorical or specialist certification held. Categorical or specialist certifications are acceptable for higher-graded positions within the relevant lab section or one of the non-section specific assignments (including, Ancillary Testing Coordinator, Education Coordinator, Laboratory Information Manager, Quality Manager, Laboratory Manager, Regional Technical Specialist, National Quality and Compliance Agent, Regional Program Manager, Regional Director, Laboratory Director, or National Quality and Compliance Officer). May qualify based on being covered by the Grandfathering Provision as described in the VA Qualification Standard for this occupation (only applicable to current VHA employees who are in this occupation and meet the criteria). GS-11 Grade Determination: Experience: 1 year of creditable experience equivalent to the next lower grade level. OR Education. Must have 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education or a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree in medical technology or a directly related science. AND Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: In addition to the experience above, the candidate must demonstrate the following KSAs: Knowledge of professional clinical laboratory science principles, practices, concepts, and theories that support sound, independent work. Knowledge of laboratory quality control and quality assurance procedures and principles of performance improvement. Skill in informatics, laboratory data flow, and laboratory processes. Ability to maintain, troubleshoot, and repair instrumentation. Ability to use independent technical judgment to analyze and interpret laboratory results. Ability to read, interpret, and apply complex written instructions. Ability to communicate, consult, and interact with other members of the health care team, external relations, customer service, and patient education. Preferred Experience: 2-5 years of experience as a CLS Generalist covering all sections in Lab including Blood bank, Chemistry/UA, Hem/Coag, Microbiology/Molecular, Quality Management, and other related duties as assigned. Understanding of regulatory compliance and Quality Management. Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/. The full performance level of this vacancy is GS-11. Physical Requirements: See VA Directive and Handbook 5019, Employee Occupational Health Service for requirements.
